I refuse to turn my supporters or my soul into fodder for the political machine. | | | Jul 29 | | | | | | | | | | | | Every election cycle, candidates are told the same thing: raise more money. Raise money to prove you are "serious." Raise money to prove you are "viable." Raise money to attract attention from institutions that will not take you seriously until you have raised enough money to pay the institutions, "con-men" aka consultants, platforms, vendors, and advertisers that determine who gets taken seriously. (And if you dare to run without paying the piper, a certain form of shark will attack your character and sabotage, malign, accuse and undermine your candidacy. Ask me how I know.) The electoral-industrial complex is a machine that repeatedly cites its own appetite as evidence of necessity. Now sure, campaigns do require money. Printing costs money. Travel costs money. Filing reports, communicating with voters, organizing volunteers, maintaining secure technology, producing materials, and reaching a large congressional district all cost money. I am sincerely grateful to every person who has entrusted this campaign with a contribution, and I am asking those who can afford to help to be among them. But money is supposed to be a tool used in service of democracy. Increasingly, American "democracy" is treated as a tool used to generate money. Around every candidate now sits an enormous electoral-industrial complex: consultants, fundraisers, polling firms, print shops, advertising companies, data brokers, texting vendors, email platforms, compliance vendors, voter-file companies, opposition researchers, media buyers, list sellers, strategists, and layer upon layer of middlemen. Some provide legitimate expertise and valuable work. Others manufacture dependency, sell candidates solutions to problems their own industry helped create, collect their overblown fees, and remain well compensated whether or not the candidate wins, the movement grows, or the public becomes any more empowered. Political consulting is one of the few industries in which the people selling the cure may also have defined the disease. The result is a closed loop. Candidates are told they must raise enormous sums to demonstrate their "viability." They must then spend those sums on the professional ecosystem that decides who appears viable. Fundraising becomes evidence of strength... because the people who live on campaign money say that fundraising is evidence of strength. The logic is insane. This circular logic has become so normalized that candidates announce fundraising totals as though the money itself were the public good they produced. But money raised is not the same as trust earned. Money spent is not the same as democracy strengthened. Payroll is not public service. Advertising is not organizing. Name recognition is not wisdom, integrity, courage, competence, or constitutional understanding. In my congressional race, another candidate has made the amount she has raised a central proof of her political strength. According to her campaign's FEC reporting, she raised approximately $609,000 and spent approximately $585,000 between April 2025 and June 2026. She ended that reporting period with about $24,000 in cash and nearly $20,000 in reported debt. Those numbers establish that her campaign can raise and consume a great deal of money. Clearly. They do not, by themselves, answer the question that matters: What durable democratic capacity existed afterward that did not exist before? What did the spending leave behind? Did it give people a deeper understanding of their government and their constitutional rights? Did it develop local leaders who will remain active after Election Day? Did it build independent civic institutions? Did it make communities less vulnerable to manipulation, surveillance, fear, and political abandonment? Did it leave voters with greater power over the decisions affecting their lives? Or did most of the activity exist only as long as the money continued moving? This is not a complaint that campaigns spend money. It is a demand that we stop mistaking financial throughput for democratic achievement. The electoral-industrial complex does not merely monetize elections. It monetizes democratic helplessness. It needs citizens to believe that every election is existential, but that their role is confined to donating, clicking, canvassing from an strictly approved script, choosing among institutionally filtered candidates, and waiting for political professionals to save them. It needs people frightened enough to give, but not empowered enough to reorganize power. That is why so much political fundraising is built around artificial emergencies, invented deadlines, catastrophic subject lines, and messages implying that democracy will collapse at midnight unless you send $17 immediately. The next morning brings another emergency, another deadline, another request and another warning that everything will be lost. When failure produces more fundraising, failure is no longer a threat to the institutions that are supposed to be responsible for winning. There is no real incentive to change behavior - to truly try to win, to learn from mistakes, to evolve strategies, to face humility, to improve... \- if failure still provides economic value. A party loses an election, and the consultants remain. A campaign burns through millions of dollars, loses, and its well-paid strategists simply move to the next campaign. Institutions repeatedly misunderstand the public, suppress strong grassroots candidates, defend unpopular incumbents, and communicate in language that ordinary people no longer trust. Then they cite the consequences of their own failures as proof that we must send them more money. It 's ludicrous. The public is told that it is the customer. Too often, the public is the product. Our money is harvested. Our fear is cultivated. Our attention is captured. Our behavior is scored. Our contact information is copied across databases and routed through companies most of us have never heard of, used for our own manipulation, and who knows what other purposes. Our names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, donation histories, interests, political views, and engagement patterns become campaign assets to be analyzed, traded, transferred, targeted, retained, and bought and sold to whoever can pay. I know. The extraction is not only financial. It is informational. I know what it feels like to donate to one campaign I believe in and suddenly find myself on fifteen other mailing lists I never joined. I do not like it. I do not believe you like it either. I will not do that to you. We carefully assess vendors, platforms, and service providers for data privacy practices. If they expose your information, or violate our trust, they're out. You won't see the normal set of tools and platforms associated with us. That's very deliberate, and it's because we respect you. I do not want our supporters' relationship with this campaign automatically hijacked into a relationship with an expansive partisan fundraising ecosystem. I wanted a platform that allowed us to maintain greater independence and exercise more control over how supporter information is handled. Why? Because we respect you. No technological platform eliminates every risk, and federal campaigns must collect and report certain contributor information under the law. But campaigns still make real choices about how many outside companies receive access to their data, how many commercial systems information passes through, and whether supporters are treated as human beings who have extended a specific trust or as names to be fed into a permanent political marketing apparatus. We have chosen to minimize that exposure wherever we can. Over the past several months, I have invested an enormous amount of my own time in building independent, non-extractive campaign operations and data systems. We run our own treasury and compliance work. We have built our own canvassing platform. We manage our own systems instead of automatically surrendering our campaign operations, supporter relationships, institutional knowledge, messaging strategy, and voter and supporter data to layers and layers of unknown, financially motivated external vendors. We have designed and built this campaign, carefully and diligently, to be maximally financially efficient, maximally independent, and as secure as we can make it. That work is not glamorous. It does not necessarily make national news. It does not generate dramatic headlines about the size of our campaign payroll. Most people will never see the hundreds - thousands ... \- of decisions involved in building an operation that does not casually expose their information, waste their money, or make itself structurally dependent on institutions whose priorities may conflict with theirs. But we do this because we respect you. We honor your trust. We understand that when you donate, volunteer, sign up, attend an event, share a message, or tell us what is happening in your life, you are not surrendering yourself to an industry. You are entering a relationship with a campaign that has an obligation to handle your money, your information, and your faith in us carefully. I am running to serve the people, not siphon from them. Unlike my opponents. That means I will raise less money than candidates who build their campaigns around relentless fundraising. That is a deliberate decision. It protects my moral integrity. It reduces donor capture. It reduces the burden I place on people who are already paying too much for housing, food, healthcare, transportation, childcare, education, and nearly every other necessity of life. It also forces discipline. When every dollar matters, spending must produce genuine value. We cannot treat our supporters as an inexhaustible reservoir that can be tapped whenever consultants want a larger budget or another layer of campaign machinery. I will not bombard people with manipulative appeals simply to feed the electoral-industrial beast. I will not manufacture panic to empty your pockets. I will not tell you that democracy will end tonight unless you respond to an arbitrary fundraising deadline. I will not measure the strength of this movement only by the amount of money passing through its accounts. I will ask for support honestly. I will tell you what it helps us accomplish. I will thank you for it. And I will use it as carefully as I know how. There is a cost to that choice. Money is genuinely useful. A campaign with more resources can communicate with more voters, print more materials, hire more people, travel more widely, withstand more attacks, and build a larger public presence. We are running to win, not to stage a symbolic protest against campaign finance. So yes: please donate if you can. But know what your contribution supports. You are not helping us become more deeply integrated into the machine. You are helping us operate independently of it. You are helping us reach people WITHOUT surrendering ourselves to the gatekeepers who claim to own the only paths by which people can be reached. You are helping us prove that political seriousness is not measured by the number of middlemen a campaign can afford. The Democratic Party apparatus . Its institutions famously protect incumbency, withhold access, narrow the definition of legitimacy, and treat grassroots democratic competition as a disruption to be contained rather than participation to be welcomed. In my case, the State Party actively tried to destroy my campaign by threatening me with a lawsuit and jail time over an accusation they knew full well was a lie. I have proof. The week in Mississippi, from The Mississippi Wire. https://us18.campaign-archive.com/?e=5703353baa&u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=e001992f9c

Wednesday, July 29, 2026 A Publication of the
Mississippi Center for Public Policy MississippiWire.News

SCHOOLS
Charter Groups Raise Concerns About Mississippi Authorizer Process; Board Approves Rules as Filed (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=charter-groups-raise-concerns-about-mississippi-authorizer-process-board-approve)
Three charter organizations asked the Mississippi Charter School Authorizer Board to judge schools on objective performance data rather than "professional judgment," and to require a full board vote before any school is placed on its intervention ladder. The board approved its revised renewal guidance and performance framework as filed.
Continue reading → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=charter-groups-raise-concerns-about-mississippi-authorizer-process-board-approve)
What is a think tank? (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=what-is-a-think-tank)
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=what-is-a-think-tank)
State Board Chairman: “We Made Those Decisions” on Troubled Teacher EFF Program (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=state-board-chairman-we-made-those-decisions-on-troubled-teacher-eff-program)
Summary: The chairman of the State Board of Education told fellow board members the board bears responsibility for problems with the state's teacher supply-fund program, after a presentation detailing a botched vendor transition and a $1.7 million overspend recovered from teachers.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=state-board-chairman-we-made-those-decisions-on-troubled-teacher-eff-program)
SIP Manufacturing to Invest More Than $100 Million in Southaven, Creating 187 Jobs (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=sip-manufacturing-to-invest-more-than-100-million-in-southaven-creating-187-jobs)
Beverage co-packer SIP Manufacturing is establishing operations in an existing Southaven building, a corporate investment of more than $100 million expected to create 187 jobs over five years, the Mississippi Development Authority announced July 22.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=sip-manufacturing-to-invest-more-than-100-million-in-southaven-creating-187-jobs)
Reeves Appoints Brad McCullouch Hinds County District Attorney; Special Election Set for November 3 (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=reeves-appoints-brad-mccullouch-hinds-county-district-attorney-special-election-)
The governor named the office's first assistant district attorney to fill the vacancy left by Jody Owens' resignation, with a special election on November 3 and a candidate qualifying deadline of August 20.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=reeves-appoints-brad-mccullouch-hinds-county-district-attorney-special-election-)
Local News
Madison County Approves One-Third Property Tax Break for $70 Million Gluckstadt Manufacturing Expansion MADISON COUNTY — Madison County supervisors approved a fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement for a $70 million manufacturing expansion in Gluckstadt — cutting the new facility’s ordinary property taxes by one-third — and heard the county is on pace to save about $140,000 after canceling its Region 8 mental health contract. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=madison-county-approves-one-third-property-tax-break-for-70-million-gluckstadt-m) Starkville Employee Heath Fund Reserve Depleted by Large Claims STARKVILLE — (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=starkville-employee-heath-fund-reserve-depleted-by-large-claims) Starkville Holds Tax Rate at 34 Mills as Reassessment Lifts Values 18–20 Percent STARKVILLE — City officials want to keep Starkville's millage at 34 mills for 2026-2027 even as a countywide reassessment pushes average assessed values up 18 to 20 percent, meaning
higher bills for many property owners. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=starkville-holds-tax-rate-at-34-mills-as-reassessment-lifts-values-18-20-percent) Southaven Projects Record $16 Million Surplus, Mayor Tells Aldermen SOUTHAVEN — Mayor Darren Musselwhite told the Board of Aldermen the city's excess surplus is projected to reach $16 million to $17 million — the highest of his tenure — though the figure awaits confirmation by independent audit. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=southaven-projects-record-16-million-surplus-mayor-tells-aldermen) Digital Tax Collections Up Roughly $600,000, Mayor Tells Council TUPELO — Mayor Todd Jordan told the city council that internet use-tax collections are up about $600,000 this year, and a Barnes Crossing drainage project came in about $400,000 under budget. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=digital-tax-collections-up-roughly-600-000-mayor-tells-council)

Schools

name: Tracinski for Congress
subject: We Need a "Project 2027"
body:
The plan to restore the power of Congress.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/916e49f1867d/why-me-17293288?e=bd44204496)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/k9EScURJptw?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a)
| | | | | |
# My Project 2027
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

[](https://us.list-manage.com/7tFKY2yvx9x?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a)

I’ve had one consistent message since I began my campaign: I think the US Congress is a good idea, and it would be nice if we had one.
We don’t have one right now. Instead, we have a bunch of lackeys who think it’s their job to trail along behind Donald Trump giving him whatever he wants—often, in the case of our Fifth District incumbent John McGuire, when Trump [hasn’t even asked](https://us.list-manage.com/9BOHPiXOb0_?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a) for Congress’s approval and doesn’t think he needs it. (See McGuire’s [bill to limit birthright citizenship](https://us.list-manage.com/13oC9kLOUlj?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a), an attempt to overturn a Supreme Court ruling by statute—which is _not_ a thing you can do.)
If we want Congress to serve as a check on the president and not a rubber stamp, then as I’ve [pointed out](https://us.list-manage.com/NhwyoNAs4cE?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a), we can’t wait for a “Project 2029.” We need to prepare for an epic showdown beginning just months from now, in January 2027. We need a Democrat in Congress who has the will to assert congressional power—and more than that, someone with a _plan_ to do it.
This is what I’ve just laid out. See my [recent article in _Liberal Currents_](https://us.list-manage.com/19YiflCzo3E?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a) on my plan for a “Project 2027.” This is not a fantasy for what we would do if we have a supermajority and the ability to amend the Constitution. This is a plan for the situation we are likely to face next January.
“Our agenda should be based on what we can do with a simple majority—and with Trump still in the White House—which is the most likely outcome of the coming election. What can we do, with just the power of a congressional majority, to rein in Trump and reform the system?”
I’ll just give the main bullet points here:
**Declare a national emergency of national emergencies.**
“We should pass a law immediately suspending _all_ emergency executive powers, requiring the president to submit such powers for review by Congress, one at a time, if he wants any of them reinstated by ordinary law.
**Take away executive discretion.**
“Congress seems to only fitfully remember that it can just _tell the executive what to do_.”
**Rediscover the power and purpose of impeachment.**
“The public won’t believe that what Trump is doing is unprecedented or an emergency or an attack on the foundations of the American system if we don’t _act_ like it is. Impeachment is our way of saying that we really mean it, that these actions are beyond the bounds of legitimate power.”
**Use the power of the purse.**
“The power of the purse is the big stick the Constitution gave us to keep the president in line.... We should make it clear that we can make the gears of the executive grind to a halt until the president makes real concessions. This is the leverage we can use to get everything else.”
[Read the whole thing.](https://us.list-manage.com/x4EjaOJHqZh?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a)
This is the big opportunity that we can salvage from the current danger to our democracy and the American system. We have an chance to build back the authority that Congress has foolishly allowed to bleed away for many decades.

If you want to help renew America’s confidence in our founding principles, support my campaign.
This is really your **last chance** to help me out before the primary on August 4, which is a week from Tuesday. Any money I’m going to spend to get over the top in the primary, I need to be spending in the next week, so please donate **now**.

---
| [DONATE TO HELP ME GET THIS IMPORTANT MESSAGE OUT](https://us.list-manage.com/rFNRBugKnYN?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a)
---
| |

### What If We Don’t Have a Plan?

I’ll be putting out a lot of more videos and articles in the final week and a half of the primary, and the point of some of them is to differentiate myself from my opponents. (For my guide to all the Fifth District candidates, of both parties, see [here](https://us.list-manage.com/g6nfB1ycJLd?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a).) Most of all, I’m trying to differentiate myself from Tom Perriello, who is Mr. Establishment among the Democrats in Charlottesville—a known and familiar face who has been a fixture of this district’s politics for years.
I get that he seems like a safe and comfortable choice. But I had an opportunity recently to point out what worries me. What if, in contrast to what I propose above—what if we don’t have a plan?
I raised this recently in [my response](https://us.list-manage.com/JTZOq6RTQDe?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a) to comments by Senator Mark Warner—who helped recruit and has endorse Perriello—in which he rules out the idea of a third impeachment of Donald Trump, as if Trump has somehow slowed down in his violations of the Constitution. But why ask voters to send us to Congress, if we don’t intend to use all the tools the Constitution gives us?
See also [my warning](https://us.list-manage.com/O7JBPSpngKe?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a) about politicians who promise to ban data centers—the latest bandwagon everyone is jumping on because the polls have flipped against Big Tech and ambitious politicians see an opportunity for grandstanding. Thirty years of covering politics have given me a sharp-edge perspective on this, and I point out that when a politician panders like this, he’s not really telling you what he thinks about data centers. He’s just telling you that he really, really wants to be in office, and he’ll tell you whatever he thinks you want to hear. This is not a good reason to vote for someone—because the moment he’s afraid the political winds are shifting, he’ll sell you out.
If you want a Democratic candidate who is running, not because he wants to feel important, but because he has a cause—if you want a candidate who actually has a _plan_ for how we put Congress back on track, then I’m your man.

Help me get this message out by[ donating with ActBlue](https://us.list-manage.com/NN8fRLZkO64?e=bd44204496&c2id=2337f871c9bdb2dd73757dd8d1ee923a). Even $100 or $200 can make a difference, especially in these crucial final days of the primary.

This is really your last chance to help me out before the primary on August 4, which is a week from Tuesday. Any money I’m going to spend to get over the top in the primary, I need to be spending in the next week, so please donate now. | | | What If We Don’t Have a Plan? I’ll be putting out a lot of more videos and articles in the final week and a half of the primary, and the point of some of them is to differentiate myself from my opponents. (For my guide to all the Fifth District candidates, of both parties, see .) Most of all, I’m trying to differentiate myself from Tom Perriello, who is Mr. Establishment among the Democrats in Charlottesville—a known and familiar face who has been a fixture of this district’s politics for years. I get that he seems like a safe and comfortable choice. But I had an opportunity recently to point out what worries me. What if, in contrast to what I propose above—what if we don’t have a plan? I raised this recently in to comments by Senator Mark Warner—who helped recruit and has endorse Perriello—in which he rules out the idea of a third impeachment of Donald Trump, as if Trump has somehow slowed down in his violations of the Constitution. But why ask voters to send us to Congress, if we don’t intend to use all the tools the Constitution gives us? See also about politicians who promise to ban data centers—the latest bandwagon everyone is jumping on because the polls have flipped against Big Tech and ambitious politicians see an opportunity for grandstanding. Thirty years of covering politics have given me a sharp-edge perspective on this, and I point out that when a politician panders like this, he’s not really telling you what he thinks about data centers. He’s just telling you that he really, really wants to be in office, and he’ll tell you whatever he thinks you want to hear. This is not a good reason to vote for someone—because the moment he’s afraid the political winds are shifting, he’ll sell you out. If you want a Democratic candidate who is running, not because he wants to feel important, but because he has a cause—if you want a candidate who actually has a plan for how we put Congress back on track, then I’m your man. Help me get this message out by. Even $100 or $200 can make a difference, especially in these crucial final days of the primary. | | | | | Please commit your support for a Congress that will not just speak for the people of this district but protect all of our rights against an out-of-control federal government. body:

**
**
**I've been going through a list of people recently who have expressed an interest in volunteering for Dr. Hardy's campaign, and your name came up.**
**
**
**I realize making calls isn't everyone's cup of tea, but before you say NO, you should know you'll be calling democrats and unaffiliated voters who lean our way who vote religiously during the presidential election years but tend to slack off during the mid-terms.**
**
**

**
**

**Michael P. Rush**

## _These prowling big cats are portraits of purr-fection!_
* * *
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s a Florida panther?_**
If you find yourself deep in the wilds of Florida, you could be lucky enough to spot a pair of yellow eyes, a tan coat, a long tail – in other words, a Florida panther!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Where can they be found?_**
Panthers are the only Puma found east of the Mississippi River. Though they once roamed throughout the Southeast, they now occupy just 5 percent of their historic range and mostly live in Southwest Florida within the Greater Everglades. These cats are also a keystone species: They play a vital role in balancing their ecosystem, and they help maintain healthy deer and feral hog populations.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_So what happened?_**
Florida panthers were nearly wiped out many years ago when early settlers arrived. Luckily, they were one of the first animals protected under the Endangered Species Act. We went from as fewer than two dozen panthers in the wild in the 1970s to up to an estimated 230 panthers today.
#
However, these big cats are still highly endangered, and their greatest threat comes from development and fragmentation of their habitat. Panthers are in grave danger as they try to cross dangerous roads that run through their habitats. They need a large range of intact swamps, forests and pinelands to hunt and raise their kittens.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can I help?_**
Panthers need allies to help protect their homes! We can make a difference by opposing developments and roads that break up vital habitat for panthers and other Florida wildlife. Wildlife corridors and crossing structures can also allow animals to safely move under highways – be sure to support these life-saving measures every chance you get. It’s a way we can all be panther protectors!
#
|
---
[Get some more panther facts!](https://support.defenders.org/s/5820147/38SyG9Xl)

Peter,

Earlier this week, on a debate stage with thousands of Michiganders
watching, my opponent lied to you.

I don't say that lightly. A moderator asked Haley Stevens a direct
question: has she taken money from DTE Energy — the utility that left
hundreds of thousands of Michiganders without power this summer? She said
no.

The receipts say otherwise. Haley Stevens did take money from DTE Energy,
over $47,000 of it. Reporters quickly fact-checked her:

[ A ]A post from a reporter saying Haley did in fact take money from DTE
Energy's PAC

That wasn't the only place her story didn't match the record
either, Peter.

She says she's tough on ICE. Her voting record says otherwise. She's voted
to fund ICE. She voted for a resolution thanking ICE agents "for
protecting the homeland" — the same ICE that's been tearing through our
neighborhoods.

She claimed to be focused on investing our tax dollars here in Michigan,
but just this month, she broke with the majority of House Democrats to
vote in favor of sending $3.3 billion in unconditional military aid to
Israel — money that could've gone toward lowering your power bill or
fixing the grid that just failed you.

Peter, we've
watched MAGA Republicans build an entire playbook out of lying to people's
faces and hoping they won't check. I'm not going to let my opponent use
that same playbook to deceive her way to the Democratic nomination and put
this must-win Senate seat at risk.

But I can’t take on this fight alone. AIPAC’s Super PACs and corporate
PACs have spent nearly $60 million to prop up our opponent and stop us,
and the only way we’ll overcome that level of spending is if we stick
together. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260729-1-ak.N_44u-&amount=10&refcode=em20260729-2762&t=1004&akid=2762%2E251025%2EWNhDUI ]Please stand with me and chip in $10 so we can

In solidarity,

Abdul

subject: Leading Republican: We can bypass Fauci’s pardon with new charges
body:
Senate Republicans subpoenaed Dr. Fauci and are weighing bringing new criminal referrals against him to try and bypass his Presidential pardon.
#
**BREAKING NEWS: Senate Republicans subpoena Dr. Anthony Fauci; force him to testify before Congress** **[Stand with Dr. Fauci ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22955?source=em20260729-1691&t=1&akid=1691%2E2118727%2ENfdbgU)**
---
Dr. Anthony Fauci served under half a dozen Presidential administrations over his 50 year career in public health.
At the height of his career, he was one of the 15 most cited scientists in the world. His leadership responding to HIV/AIDS, Ebola, SARS, Covid-19, and vaccine preventable diseases is credited with saving upwards of 30 million lives.
**Dr. Fauci is a public health hero – and at 85 years old should be allowed to enjoy his retirement.**
But he can’t. GOP Sen. Rand Paul subpoenaed him to substantiate his deranged conspiracy theories around Covid, the Chair of the House Oversight Committee warned Republicans could bypass Fauci’s pardon with new criminal charges, and he spent the morning being attacked and dogpiled by anti-science Republicans.
The Republican Party has never been more unpopular so they are looking for a scapegoat, a distraction, a new target: **And Dr. Fauci is that new target.**
**We want to show Dr. Anthony Fauci that the American people have his back:[Will you take 60 seconds today to stand with Dr. Fauci against these outrageous attacks?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22955?source=em20260729-1691&t=2&akid=1691%2E2118727%2ENfdbgU)**

Today, New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement on the passing of Hon. Fred Doucette

**Chairman Maltzie on the Passing of Hon. Fred Doucette**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** July 29th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |
**CONCORD, N.H.** — Today, New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement on the passing of Hon. Fred Doucette:“I was deeply saddened to learn of Fred's passing this morning. Throughout his life, Fred dedicated himself to serving both our state and our nation, and I had the privilege of witnessing firsthand the impact of his leadership and unwavering commitment to New Hampshire.Fred first answered the call to serve as a United States Navy Corpsman before continuing his commitment to public safety as a firefighter, paramedic, and Station Commander for the Town of Salem, New Hampshire.His dedication to public service led him to the New Hampshire House of Representatives, where he served six terms. During his tenure, he held several key leadership positions, including Assistant Majority Leader, Deputy Majority Leader, and Speaker Pro Tempore. He earned the respect of his colleagues through his steady leadership, integrity, and dedication to serving the people of New Hampshire.Fred also exemplified what it meant to be a Republican leader. He served as New Hampshire co-chair for President Donald Trump's 2016 and 2020 campaigns, helping lead two successful efforts in the Granite State.His decades of service did not go unnoticed. President Donald Trump appointed Fred as the Region I Administrator for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), where he continued his lifelong commitment to serving others.I will remember Fred not only for the many positions he held, but for the character he displayed in each one. He lived a life defined by service, leadership, and love for New Hampshire. On behalf of the New Hampshire Republican Party, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his wife, family, friends, and all those who had the privilege of knowing him. His legacy will live on in the countless lives he touched, and he will be deeply missed.”

News just broke that a detention center planned for North Carolina will be one of the largest on the entire East Coast.

# [The Electoral-Industrial Complex (I Reject)](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=208870430&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4ODcwNDMwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODUzMzk5NDgsImV4cCI6MTc4NzkzMTk0OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.C2L-2Z9QDf0ZWnQoXYJNauqeT92hKY2xTiMGPSsdBrI)
### Politics isn't supposed to be an industry.
| | [Melissa Chaudhry](https://substack.com/@melissa4congress)

Every election cycle, the first thing they tell candidates is: raise more money. Raise it to look "serious." Raise it to look "viable." Raise it, in short, to pay the very consultants who decide who's serious and who's viable in the first place. Yes, it's that circular. Yes, it's that ridiculous.
Here's the truth nobody says out loud: fundraising isn't proof a campaign is strong. Fundraising is proof a campaign is feeding the industry that surrounds it -- consultants, pollsters, digital marketers, data brokers, ad buyers, layer after layer of people who get paid whether you win or lose. They don't need your campaign to succeed. They just need it to spend.
When a campaign fails, they don't lose a thing. They just move to the next one. Unlike any respectable industry -- but very much like war -- failure isn't a threat to the machine. Failure is itself a product line.
**Money raised is not trust earned. Money spent is not democracy strengthened.**
So here's what I won't do:
-- I won't blast you with fake deadlines at 2 AM
-- I won't tell you "democracy ends tonight unless you send $17 right now"
-- I won't sell your name, your email, your history to 15 lists you never joined
-- No corporate PACs. No foreign interests. No defense contractors. No data profiteering.
I've spent months -- quiet, diligent months -- building this campaign to run on its own systems. Because you are not a name to be harvested. You are a person who trusted me.
* * *
Last time I ran, in 2024, nobody thought I was viable. No money, no name recognition. When the machine finally noticed I was compelling to people, it treated me as a threat. My own party tried to kill my campaign with threats and lawsuits -- over a lie they knew was a lie. I can prove it.
I won my primary anyway.
I ran in the general against an AIPAC-funded 30-year incumbent. I conducted voter outreach in 14 languages. I distributed most of a million pieces of literature. I earned over 90,000 votes.
Then last year, ICE illegally abducted my husband -- a decorated, disabled American military veteran in a wheelchair -- right out of his own citizenship appointment. We had no lawyers. No money. I fought simultaneously in 4 federal courts against ICE, DHS, the DOJ, and the Attorney General of the United States.
After 4 grueling months, a federal judge ordered his immediate release, calling the detention flat out wrong.
That taught me something about power -- how it hides, and what it takes to defeat it.
* * *
I know exactly what these machines are built to do to people. I was thrown into that with no warning and no protection. I still came out victorious, with my soul intact.
These machines are made to look imposing, inevitable, merciless -- like the sole arbiter of truth and justice. They're not. They're weak, shallow, contradictory, and honestly an embarrassment to humanity.
We don't need to bow before them.
I will not turn my supporters into fodder for a fundraising industry. I will not turn my soul into fodder for a political one.
Let me be the one clear diamond the machine chokes on -- and let's see what you and I can build together.
**Care, courage, the Constitution.**
🗳️ Vote Melissa for Congress -> www.VoteMelissa4Congress.com

My bill, the Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act, just passed the House Ways and Means Committee with the support of Chairman Jason Smith. Tax-exempt organizations would be barred from contributing to political committees for two years after taking a gift from a foreign national. That covers both charitable groups and the social welfare organizations that can pump unlimited money into Super PACs. And if a group breaks the rule three times? They lose their tax-exempt status for two years.
---
Our elections should be decided by American voters, not by foreign billionaires who move money through a network of nonprofits to influence our democracy.

clean_body: Friends, Foreign money has no business in American elections. Yet there's a loophole that lets foreign nationals funnel cash through nonprofit organizations and into our political system. | Friends, Foreign money has no business in American elections. Yet there's a loophole that lets foreign nationals funnel cash through nonprofit organizations and into our political system. I did something about it. | My bill, the Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act, just passed the House Ways and Means Committee with the support of Chairman Jason Smith. Tax-exempt organizations would be barred from contributing to political committees for two years after taking a gift from a foreign national. That covers both charitable groups and the social welfare organizations that can pump unlimited money into Super PACs. And if a group breaks the rule three times? They lose their tax-exempt status for two years. Our elections should be decided by American voters, not by foreign billionaires who move money through a network of nonprofits to influence our democracy. | The bill now heads to the full House floor. I'm going to keep fighting to get it across the finish line, but I need you standing with me. | | | | | | Thank you, Nicole | Nicole for New York, PO Box 60487, Staten Island, NY 10306

# Iran
* **Iran launches missiles toward U.S. base in Jordan** : Iran [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/fbcddb47-1428-4735-aeb7-5022f3771a44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ballistic missiles toward a U.S. base in Jordan on Tuesday evening and Wednesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps confirmed, with U.S. and Jordanian military officials [claiming](https://substack.com/redirect/cdbed17a-6045-4350-a2af-b37d07fbf30e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the missiles were intercepted.
* After an initial announcement by the U.S. that it had shot down a series of missile attacks on Tuesday evening, the Jordanian military said it had intercepted 5 missiles on Wednesday morning.
* In a statement confirming the attacks, the IRGC said that the attacks targeted Muwaffaq Salti Air Base and the headquarters of the U.S. military's Central Command in Jordan and [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/1743fc96-42ff-45ac-b054-2e7150c5f01c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that they would continue as long as U.S. threats and actions against Iranian interests persist.
* In [remarks](https://substack.com/redirect/e6dd6b4c-4e6a-4629-ac6b-a782f00a5ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Fox News, Trump said, "We're going to beat the fuc*ing sh*t out of them. We'll be hitting them hard," adding that Iran was "going to get a beating," in response to the attack. He said U.S. troops had only minutes to respond before intercepting the missiles. Trump also said that Washington would "let them keep talking" regarding the possibility of future negotiations with Tehran.
* Iranian state television reported Wednesday that U.S. warplanes carried out airstrikes on an area near the Iraqi border in northwestern Iran, saying a location in the border region of Piranshahr came under "hostile U.S. airstrikes." Earlier, the semi-official Fars news agency quoted the crisis management chief of West Azerbaijan province as saying a "hostile missile" struck an uninhabited area in the same region, causing no casualties.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran launches missiles toward U.S. base in Jordan : Iran ballistic missiles toward a U.S. base in Jordan on Tuesday evening and Wednesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps confirmed, with U.S. and Jordanian military officials that the missiles were intercepted. After an initial announcement by the U.S. that it had shot down a series of missile attacks on Tuesday evening, the Jordanian military said it had intercepted 5 missiles on Wednesday morning. In a statement confirming the attacks, the IRGC said that the attacks targeted Muwaffaq Salti Air Base and the headquarters of the U.S. military's Central Command in Jordan and that they would continue as long as U.S. threats and actions against Iranian interests persist. In to Fox News, Trump said, "We're going to beat the fucing sht out of them. We'll be hitting them hard," adding that Iran was "going to get a beating," in response to the attack. He said U.S. troops had only minutes to respond before intercepting the missiles. Trump also said that Washington would "let them keep talking" regarding the possibility of future negotiations with Tehran. Iranian state television reported Wednesday that U.S. warplanes carried out airstrikes on an area near the Iraqi border in northwestern Iran, saying a location in the border region of Piranshahr came under "hostile U.S. airstrikes." Earlier, the semi-official Fars news agency quoted the crisis management chief of West Azerbaijan province as saying a "hostile missile" struck an uninhabited area in the same region, causing no casualties. U.S.-Saudi Strikes across Iraq kill at least 20 PMF fighters: Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) joint U.S.-Saudi airstrikes killed at least 20 of its fighters and wounded 32 others in attacks across seven provinces, in one of the biggest escalations in the region in weeks. The PMF, an Iraqi state-integrated paramilitary body with factions close to Tehran, said the strikes hit its positions in Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, and Diyala, damaging buildings, vehicles, and equipment. U.S. Central Command and Saudi Arabia confirmed the joint operation, saying it targeted "Iran-backed" militants in retaliation for attacks on U.S. troops and Saudi oil facilities, with CENTCOM saying it hit "logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq." Trump claimed the overnight strikes were carried out in coordination with the Iraqi government. Earlier on Tuesday, Saudi Arabia its air defenses had intercepted and destroyed additional drones targeting petroleum facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh, following separate attacks reported Monday and Tuesday. Riyadh blamed Iran-aligned militias operating from Iraqi territory. Iraq's National Security Council, chaired by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, the U.S.-Saudi strikes, calling the attack "an unacceptable aggression," the Iraqi News Agency reported. The council said the strikes came while Baghdad was communicating with U.S. and Saudi officials to address concerns over attacks on Saudi territory. It announced a comprehensive security plan to "confront any violation of Iraq's sovereignty" and stressed that responding to such attacks is "the exclusive responsibility of the Iraqi government and its constitutional institutions." Iraqi militias deny responsibility for Saudi attacks: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella of "resistance axis"-aligned factions, involvement in the drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities that Riyadh has blamed on Iraq on Tuesday, calling the accusations "fabrications." The group said the claims were meant to mask Saudi Arabia's "inability to respond to the painful Yemeni strikes," and warned that any "foolish action" by the kingdom would meet a "harsh response." Yemen's Ansarallah has separately claimed the attacks on Saudi, with spokesman Yahya Saree saying they targeted crude facilities in the kingdom's east. Netanyahu visits Trump: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House on Tuesday for a closed-door meeting, which lasted roughly an hour and a half and was described by White House officials as "positive and productive." At the meeting's conclusion, Netanyahu he had finished "one of the best conversations I've ever had with a president of the United States, our friend Donald Trump." After their meeting, Netanyahu was by Fox News' Sean Hannity, and said about the U.S.-Israel war on Iran that he was "skeptical" of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding and that Israel would respond "with terrific force" if attacked by Iran. He said he and Trump "see...eye to eye" on this, and were both committed to preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons. Trump a different tone when he was interviewed by Fox News on Tuesday, telling Fox & Friends that he was frustrated that his plans to discuss intelligence regarding an alleged nuclear facility at Iran's "Pickaxe Mountain" with Netanyahu were leaked. "I don't need [Netanyahu] to tell me that," he said, expressing a similar frustration that Netanyahu insisted that the U.S. "stay involved" in the war. Iranian deputy FM on Hormuz, U.S. blockade, and Iran 's nuclear program: Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran's deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, Tehran's strategic position during an appearance on Iranian state television on Tuesday. Iran insists, Gharibabadi says, on control of the Strait of Hormuz, which it says will "never return" to the prewar status quo. "If the Strait of Hormuz returns to its previous arrangements, our success in the war will not be complete." Iran will keep the Strait closed unless Oman agrees to a new arrangement handing Tehran control over the waterway's shipping lanes, Gharibabadi said. Gharibabadi also noted that Iran is prepared to keep the Strait closed, even if it means war resumes, and that it would never recognize the southern shipping lane that the U.S. and Oman have proposed and attempted to establish. He warned the U.S. against its present strategy of imposing a naval blockade on the country, saying that it would not force any concessions on Iran's part, and said that any European warship approaching the Strait would be considered a legitimate military target by Iran. On the nuclear issue, Gharibabadi said Iran is effectively operating as if it were no longer a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), adding that it rejects inspections by the International Atomic Energy Agency and other international agencies as long as the war continues. "The other side should not think Iran will remain in the NPT forever. All options are on the table," he said. Traffic still impacted through Hormuz, though no new attacks reported: The Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) said on Tuesday that the regional maritime threat level in the Gulf remained "Severe," but reported no newly confirmed attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz during the past 48 hours. Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains well below normal, with most transits continuing through the northern Iranian-controlled corridor. JMIC said IRGC harassment of merchant vessels, including hailing, drone overflights, and surveillance, persists, while many ships continue sailing with AIS switched off after earlier attacks. The maritime tracking firm Kpler only seven total transits through Hormuz yesterday (another firm, Windward, five). Iran's IRGC Navy on Tuesday that it targeted and stopped three oil tankers that continued along what it called an unsafe and illegal route despite repeated warnings. Iran demands restitution over Ukrainian strike on ship Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi Tuesday he had been assured by his Ukrainian counterpart, Andrii Sybiha, that a Ukrainian attack on an Iranian commercial ship was "unintentional" and that Kyiv was not seeking escalation. Araghchi called any attack on Iranian citizens or interests "unacceptable" and demanded "restitution for losses." The Ukrainian strike on Saturday killed one Iranian sailor and wounded another, according to Iran's Foreign Ministry. Yemen Ansarallah reports successful downing of Saudi reconnaissance drone: Yemen's Armed Forces, the military wing of the Ansarallah movement, on Wednesday that it shot down a Saudi Karayel reconnaissance drone while it was carrying out "hostile operations" over the Saada governorate in northern Yemen, near the Saudi border. The Karayel-SU is a Turkish-designed military drone used for surveillance, intelligence gathering and target identification, though it can also carry guided weapons. Spokesperson Yahya Saree the drone was downed and asserted that Yemeni forces would continue "defending the country's sovereignty" by responding to any further attacks. China holds direct talks with Ansarallah for Bab Al-Mandab access: China direct talks with Yemen's Ansarallah movement to secure safe passage for Chinese tankers through the Bab Al-Mandab Strait after the group announced it would target vessels calling on Saudi ports, Reuters reported on Tuesday. Chinese officials are reportedly clearing tankers individually with Ansarallah, while informing Iran of each transit. At least four China-bound tankers have made the passage since the blockade was announced. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed--one in a new attack and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 29 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,335 killed, with 174,052 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,209 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,943, while 803 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks on Gaza kill one, wound 29: Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Tuesday at least one Palestinian and wounded 29 others, according to the Palestinian news agency WAFA. An Israeli attack on the Al-Balata Market in the Nuseirat refugee camp killed a Palestinian man and wounded 20 others. An Israeli drone struck the roof of a residential building in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood, wounding three. Israeli forces shot and wounded two more Palestinians east of Deir al-Balah. Four Palestinians were wounded by Israeli fire in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis. Additionally, Israeli forces destroyed the Dar Al-Muttaqin Mosque in the Yarmouk area of central Gaza City, leveling tents sheltering displaced people beside it, and issued several forced displacement orders in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City preceding Tuesday's wave of strikes. Israeli settlers, forces continue to ravage the occupied West Bank: Israeli forces a house in the town of Naalin, west of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to Arab48. The house, which was constructed during the late Ottoman era, was more than 120 years old. Israeli forces demolished at least 13 Palestinian homes across the West Bank this week alone, according to the IMEMC news agency. Israeli authorities more than 22 dunums--an area roughly equal to the size of four football fields--of Palestinian land near Jenin in the northern occupied West Bank, the Palestinian Information Center reported on Tuesday. Israeli settlers destroyed a vehicle belonging to a Palestinian man in Beit Ula on Tuesday, kidnapping him and another passenger, WAFA . In a separate incident on Tuesday evening in the Bethlehem district, Israeli settlers to a Palestinian man's vehicle after attacking his home. Israeli undercover forces disguised in civilian clothing a 55-year-old Palestinian man in the abdomen and foot during a raid on the town of Beit Ummar, north of Hebron, on Wednesday, according to WAFA. The forces also surrounded a home in the area and arrested a Palestinian man. Israeli settlers 20 citrus trees on a Palestinian farm in Wada Qana on Wednesday morning, WAFA reported. In the Tubas area, Israeli forces to destroy an artesian well used by Palestinian families in the area, WAFA reported. The well had previously been rendered inoperable by Israeli attacks, endangering the agricultural endeavors of the area, which are suffering under Israel's "Crimson Thread," a project to build a military road and separation wall in the area. UNHCR: Attacks by Israeli settlers "hitting an all-time high": The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said attacks on Palestinians by Israeli settlers and the expansion of settlements and outposts are "hitting an all-time high" in the occupied West Bank. "We are alarmed by the Israeli government's announcement to further increase the number of settlements and outposts, and open calls by Israeli leaders for revenge and collective punishment against Palestinian communities, accompanied by threats to turn the West Bank into another Gaza," Ravina Shamdasani, UNHCR spokesperson said in a statement on Wednesday. Palestinian man accused of carrying out "shooting attack" was shot while unarmed, video shows: Sheikh Farouk Ramadan, a Palestinian whom Israel a "terrorist" after he defended himself during a confrontation with armed settlers in the occupied West Bank village of Tal on Friday, was shot dead while unarmed, an analysis of four videos by +972 Magazine and Local Call found. The report confirms that Ramadan did wrestle away a settler's rifle and that he fired it during their interaction. Videos then show him walking slowly towards soldiers, unarmed and with nothing in his hands, before dropping to the ground. He was shot dead in this position, possibly by a settler, minutes after the gun had left his hands. Lebanon Israeli ceasefire violations continue in southern Lebanon: Israeli forces to homes in the village of Qantara in Marjayoun district, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli soldiers also the Ali Al-Taher hill on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa. In Tyre (Sour) district, Israeli forces the remaining homes in villages across the western sector before dawn, particularly in the Al-Masha area of Mansouri. Israel accuses Hezbollah of ceasefire breach: Israel Hezbollah of committing a "blatant violation" of the Lebanon ceasefire, alleging the group launched an explosive drone at an Israeli military engineering vehicle in the Ali Al-Taher area of occupied southern Lebanon overnight, The Times of Israel reported. The Israeli military said no injuries were reported and that its troops would continue operating in the area. Israel is currently deliberating a response to the incident, according to security officials. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com U.S. News Senate advances bipartisan Russia sanctions bill: The Senate 86-12 Tuesday to advance a bipartisan measure imposing sweeping sanctions on Russia and Iran, named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham , who died earlier this month while working to secure the bill's passage. The bill imposes harsh new penalties on countries that purchase oil and other energy products from Russia and expands existing sanctions against Iran. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy watched from the gallery after meeting with senators. 11 Democrats and one Republican voted against the bill. ICE document confirms forced feeding of hunger striker in detention : An ICE Health Service Corps document reviewed by The Guardian the Trump administration forcibly treated at least one immigrant detention hunger striker between October and December of last year, using methods that could include force-feeding, hydration, or involuntary catheterization or blood draws. The disclosure, produced in response to Senate appropriations committee reporting requirements, comes as hundreds of detainees have staged hunger strikes at facilities including Delaney Hall in New Jersey and Adelanto in California. Forced feeding has been condemned by international human rights groups and medical associations as a form of torture. Senate confirms Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence : The Senate Jay Clayton , the U.S. attorney in Manhattan, to lead the Office of the Director of National Intelligence in a 51-47 party-line vote on Tuesday. Democratic support eroded after Clayton gave evasive answers during his confirmation hearing about whether President Joe Biden won the 2020 election. Sen. Mark Warner(D-Va.) said he hoped Clayton would prove more stable than acting director Bill Pulte , who claimed Tuesday to have executed a "5th and Near Final Round of TERMINATIONS" totaling a 30% staff reduction during his brief tenure. Fauci invokes the Fifth Amendment: Anthony Fauci , former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination in response to questions from the Senate Homeland Security Committee Tuesday about his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic. Fauci, who was pardoned by President Joe Biden, accused Sen. Rand Paul(R-Ky.)** of having an "unhinged obsession with me." Paul released 11,000 pages of Fauci's unredacted personal diary over the weekend, in which his observations often directly contradicted his public messaging about the virus. Beshear calls out McConnell for concealing health status: Kentucky** Gov. Andy Beshear publicly that Sen. Mitch McConnell prove he remains capable of serving or resign, after 43 days without voting or directly addressing constituents following his hospitalization. After writing a letter to McConnell on Monday, Beshear called upon Sen. John Thune to "fully investigate" McConnell's health condition and his ability to serve Kentuckians. August 3 may be the cutoff date after which Beshear cannot call a special election, Beshear noted during a Tuesday appearance on Bloomberg. Other International News Cholera outbreak in Sudan: Cholera has at least 170 people and infected more than 2,000 in Sudan since May, with the Kordofan region hit hardest, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Relief agencies are racing to respond despite severe obstacles set by the country's ongoing civil war, setting up nearly 80 monitoring sites, 16 treatment centers, and eight rehydration facilities, and reaching more than 270,000 people with prevention efforts. OCHA warned the response is crippled by a funding shortfall, with Sudan's 2026 humanitarian appeal raising just $1.1 billion of the $2.9 billion needed. Ukrainian drones strike refineries and logistics sites across Russia: Ukraine launched overnight using long-range drones on oil refineries in Perm and Ryazan, a Ryazan logistics center, an export terminal and military plant in Rostov, and a Russian naval base in occupied Crimea, President Zelenskyy said in a statement announcing the strikes. A warehouse for the company Wildberries in Ryazan was evacuated after catching fire. The online retailer, known as the Russian equivalent to Amazon, said that a recent campaign of Ukrainian strikes targeting its facilities have damaged at least seven warehouses in recent days, eliminating roughly 10 percent of its storage capacity. Ukraine claims that the company provides components for Russian attack drones. Russia, meanwhile, struck Kherson, killing one person, and said its drones hit two vessels carrying weapons and military equipment near Odessa. Russia charges Telegram founder with aiding terrorism : Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity and placed him on an international wanted list, alleging that Ukrainian intelligence used a dating chatbot on the platform to recruit young Russians for attacks on security personnel and infrastructure. The FSB said 46 Russians ages 12 to 22 had been arrested over the past year after being recruited through the chatbot. Telegram is popular in Russia and used by Russian defense and government agencies for public communications, though Moscow has begun throttling access to the platform in response to concerns over its use for foreign espionage. UN report: Boeing 727s linked to U.S. contractor supplied RSF in Sudan: A draft UN report that Boeing 727s linked to a business network involving former U.S. Army Special Forces contractor Steven Shaulis transported mercenaries, weapons and drones for Sudan's Rapid Support Forces via an N'Djamena-Nyala air corridor, according to Reuters. The report also detailed the scale of support from an estimated 1,500-2,000 Colombian mercenaries known as the Desert Wolves, hired by UAE-based firm Global Security Services Group, who fought alongside the RSF during its siege of El-Fasher, violence the UN has said amounted to genocide. Five Kenyan security officers killed in clash with al-Shabaab : Five Kenyan security officers were Tuesday when a patrol team clashed with suspected al-Shabaab militants near Wantey Dam in Mandera county, close to the Somali border, according to Reuters. Police said they are pursuing the militants after a reinforcement team's armored vehicle was destroyed by an improvised explosive device, though no casualties were reported from this attack. Thousands protest against third presidential term in Congo: Thousands Tuesday in the M23-controlled cities of Goma and Bukavu against proposed constitutional changes that could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term, Reuters reported, following Congo's parliament approving a bill in June to submit such changes to a referendum. * * *
I remain utterly flummoxed and angry that virtually no one in the Republican Party has called for Ohio Congressman Max Miller to resign and drop out of his race.
Miller is credibly accused of beating his ex-wife -- holding a gun to her head, pushing her against a wall and hitting her head, and fracturing their young daughter's collarbone. He is a disgusting human being and should not be representing anybody in the United States Congress. Full stop.
Miller felt comfortable putting his hands on his wife and his child because he knows there's no accountability -- he's never going to see the inside of a prison cell, and his relationship with Donald Trump keeps him safe and the rest of the party in line. This isn't even his first public accusation of domestic abuse, yet the entire GOP supporting his initial run for Congress. He knew then what he knows now: none of it would ever touch him. That is gross.
Worse still, the woman making these latest allegations, Emily Moreno, is the daughter of a sitting Republican senator, Bernie Moreno -- and even her own father has been largely silent. Miller ran unopposed in his primary and is on the ballot again this November, and the entire party has decided the smart play is to look away and hope you don't notice.
And remember how brazen this has always been. Years ago, on the floor of the House -- during his _own_ expulsion, of all things -- George Santos, of all people, called Max Miller an accused woman beater to his face. "We all have pasts," Santos said. Nobody batted an eye. Maybe because Santos was a joke. Either way, the party shrugged and moved on -- and it's still shrugging.
I want to be clear about my own record, because it matters. I was one of the first to say Eric Swalwell should resign over the allegations against him. I was one of the first to say Graham Platner should drop out of the Maine Senate race -- and frankly, I wish I'd said it sooner. A lot of Democrats do, given that he was a living, breathing red flag.
* * *

* * *
That's the whole point. The Democratic Party lives by an entirely different set of rules. We are still tethered to reality; we still care about removing predators from our own party. The Republicans simply don't, and they _can 't_, because the top of the food chain in their party is a predator. Donald Trump was found liable for sexually abusing E. Jean Carroll, ordered to pay her millions, and still owes her a fortune. That's before the Epstein files, or the thousands of times he went on the Howard Stern show and said creepy, disgusting things about young women, including his own daughter.
You can't demand accountability from Max Miller when the man at the head of your party is the walking example of everything you'd be condemning. So they say nothing. "The key word there is _allegation_ ," they tell you, and they move on.
And make no mistake about why. For them it's party over principle, party over country, every single time. They won't police their own because all they care about is winning and owning the libs, and they're reflexively loyal to everyone in the party no matter what he's done. Here's the tell: they can see it perfectly well when the accused is a Democrat. They were happy to spend weeks hammering Graham Platner, demanding he get out of his race. But Max Miller -- their guy? Suddenly the outrage evaporates and everybody's very interested in due process. The standard was never the conduct. It's the letter next to your name.
And if you think Miller is somehow the exception, look at how many Republicans are falling over themselves for the Tate brothers -- Andrew and Tristan -- sitting in a Florida jail cell fighting extradition to the U.K. on rape and sex-trafficking charges brought by women who say they were abused and coerced. A whole ecosystem on the right is openly campaigning to spring them, working every connection it can find into Trump's orbit. The rest are just praying nobody asks, because they don't want their base screaming at them for admitting an accused sex trafficker maybe shouldn't be their guy. That's how broken this is -- unfathomably, unforgivably disgusting.
But this is bigger than Max Miller. The wealthy and well-connected never face accountability for their crimes or their corruption, because they built the system that way. They draw their own districts, so they don't answer to voters. They've got tens of millions in super-PAC money waiting, from AIPAC and shit like that. And they know Trump's DOJ won't touch them. So when a president launches an illegal war and nobody cares, when a sitting United States senator vanishes for six weeks and nobody in Washington blinks, when the Epstein files can't and won't be released in violation of the law -- it's always the same answer. There's no gravity in Washington anymore. They protect one another across every scandal, because the only bipartisan consensus left in that town is that none of them should ever pay a price.
So here's where I land. The gravity in this country isn't coming back from Washington -- they've spent decades engineering it out. It has to come from us -- from people who still believe a man who holds a gun to his wife's head has no business writing our laws, who refuse to accept _allegation_ as a magic word that makes accountability disappear. It angers the hell out of me, all of it, because it just isn't right. So no, I'm not going to let it go -- not with Miller, not with the Tates, not with any of them. Demand it loudly. Demand it until it costs them something. Because the day we stop demanding it is the day the last ounce of the gravity leaves the country.

The newest polling for my race against Greg Abbott shows us within**just three points at** 42% to 45%** -- that's statistically tied**. To put this milestone in perspective, when Beto O'Rourke ran against Abbott in 2022, the closest margin he ever got was 5 points, and we're already inside that.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/289138a4-f97a-4c7a-b962-e371bc55ec48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We're only gaining momentum now. The very same poll showed this was a 5-point race in May at 41% to 46%. And this is the _second_ poll to show us within three points of Abbott. Texans are clearly ready for change.
Poll after poll shows Greg Abbott is the least popular he's ever been in his political career. Every indicator shows this is the year we can unseat him! _No more pay-to-play and no more data center handouts._
**Texans are tired of paying more and getting less.**
Greg Abbott has run the state of Texas for more than a decade, and it's NOT possible to overstate the damage he has done. He is single handedly destroying our neighborhood schools with his voucher scam. He is handing our communities over to massive data centers that seize land and guzzle up our water supply while we foot the bill. Time and again, he's put the interests of billionaire donors ahead of hardworking Texans, leaving us all paying the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax. That's why it's harder to make it in Texas after 12 years of Greg Abbott.
**It 's past time for new leadership in Texas.**
We are all in the same boat. It's 99% of us who are up against the interests of billionaire donors. That is the one fight of 2026. It is the fight of our time. Is this going to be a Texas that is by and for the people or is this the billionaire world and we just live here?
And because 10% of voters remain undecided, you better believe that between now and Election Day, my team and I will continue driving across our beautiful state meeting and talking with voters, knocking on doors, and sharing our vision for a Texas where the future is ours.
_I am running to bring back the American Dream: to save Texas schools and put money in your pocket. We will end the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax and build the future all Texans deserve._
**This newly released poll proves that the momentum is on our side.** Texans see Abbott's corruption and are ready to fight back. They know that Abbott is working for his donors and not Texans.
Three points isn't a guarantee. It's an opportunity. Opportunities like this don't come around often, and they certainly don't happen on their own. We still have millions of voters to reach, thousands of doors to knock, and communities across Texas to organize before Election Day.
**[If you 're ready to bring this fight all the way to November, please consider chipping in $5, $10, or whatever you can today to power this momentum.](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f81157-cde7-4f3c-a1cf-50628abb81d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
It's time we come together and fight back. Texas is our home, and we get to decide what happens here.
Let's win this.
-- Gina

body:
Big Tech's data centers, Washington's fraud — and you get handed the bill. Not anymore.
| [ MELANIE LUCERO
FOR CONGRESS · VIRGINIA'S 5TH DISTRICT ](https://us.list-manage.com/_jGyPM4J7w2?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)
---
Where I stand · Affordability
# You didn't order any of this. You just got handed the check.
Peter,Everywhere I go on this campaign — county fairs, church parking lots, front porches across the 5th District — I hear the same math problem: the grocery bill that jumped, the power bill that doubled, the mortgage rate that priced a family out of the home they earned. The math stopped working — and it's not your fault.Start with that power bill. Virginia is the data center capital of the world, and our own state watchdog says that if data center growth goes unchecked, power demand here will **double within ten years** — driven by Big Tech's server farms — with a typical Dominion customer projected to pay **$14 to $37 more every month by 2040** for the privilege. The regional grid auction that sets our capacity prices jumped nearly tenfold in 2024, and it has closed at the price cap in every auction since. You didn't order any of that. You just got handed the check.Virginia's own regulators already saw this coming. They approved a separate rate class for the very largest power users, so data centers carry more of their own costs instead of spreading them across your bill. Our state moved. Congress hasn't.So let me be plain about the standard I'll vote for: **if you build a data center, you bring your own power.** You don't ride the grid your neighbors paid for, and you don't hand them the bill for the privilege. I'll put my name on any bill that gets us there, and then I'll go find the votes to pass it.So here's my challenge to my opponent: say where you stand on that standard, in writing, before August 4. Because talking about affordability in a press release while families choose between groceries and the light bill — that's not representing the 5th District. That's decorating it.And while your bill goes up, Washington loses up to **$521 billion a year to fraud** — the government's own number. Every dollar of fraud, every useless program nobody can defend, is a dollar that came out of your paycheck. Killing that waste isn't some Washington accounting exercise. It's money back in the pockets of the 5th District.I'm also sick of the tone. You've heard it too: _" Pay more in taxes — or else." "Follow our rules — or else." "Don't ask questions about our fraud — or else."_ Since when does the government get to threaten the people who pay for all of it? Let me remind Washington of something the Marine Corps taught me on day one: you work for the people in front of you. Not the other way around.My plan is the Trump plan: cut the spending, kill the fraud, cut taxes, unleash American energy, and make Big Tech pay its own bills. The American Dream isn't a luxury item — and I won't let Washington price you out of it.I help families reach that dream for a living. Let me fight for it in Congress. | [See The Full Plan](https://us.list-manage.com/zibyyuRlS2o?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)

The film industry is incredibly important to California, so I want to talk through exactly what this merger would mean — and why we’re asking the court to step in and block it:
Paramount Skydance is already massive. If their merger with Warner Bros. Discovery goes through, one industry titan would own two of Hollywood’s major film distributors and two of the major basic cable channel owners.
The combined corporation would control nearly one-third of all theatrical motion pictures, and nearly one-third of basic cable TV programming — a clear violation of antitrust law.
If you want to support our work enforcing antitrust law and holding powerful corporations accountable to the law, please contribute any amount today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
With this merger, Paramount and Warner Bros. would be able to snuff out competition, drive up prices, diminish content quality, and create fewer films and television shows each year.
We have antitrust laws for a reason: competition fuels innovation. Think of Titanic, The Godfather, Casablanca, Harry Potter ... who knows what these movies would have been like if not for the competition driving these distributors to produce their very best work?
The film industry has the power to bring us together, and in California it's a source of immense pride — and employment — up and down the state. The industry exists to tell stories, to spark ideas and curiosity, to inspire and inform, and to open our eyes to new perspectives.
It doesn’t exist to create monopolies that drive up prices and drive down consumer choice.
I’m suing Paramount and Warner Bros. to block this merger, make sure antitrust laws are enforced, and protect consumers in California and across the country.
If you’re with me, will you help power our work with a contribution right now? No amount is too small — anything you can give has a real impact on what we can accomplish together. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20260729_GlovesOff&akid=177%2E344797%2EX2Lesl ]COURIER Newsroom

Hey Peter, it's Tara McGowan.

Within four months, two of the Democratic Party's fastest rising stars
watched their campaigns fall apart. Eric Swalwell ended his campaign for
California Governor.

Graham Platner suspended his Maine Senate bid in July, days before he was
set to take on Susan Collins.

Both men denied the allegations against them. Both campaigns ended anyway.

And the same attorney was in the room for both.

On this week's episode of Gloves Off, I sat down with Cheyenne Hunt, the
attorney and organizer who founded Reckoning Action, the group built to
support survivors of sexual assault and workplace abuse and to verify
their accounts before they go public:

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/577?t=1003&refcode=20260729_GlovesOff&akid=177%2E344797%2EX2Lesl ]Watch the full episode →

Cheyenne helped gather and substantiate Jenny Racicot's account before
Politico ran it. We talked about what that process actually looks like,
what it costs the women who come forward, and why the "perfect victim"
myth still decides who gets believed.

Gloves Off only exists because our grassroots donors understand the
urgency of supporting independent media and conversations like this.

I want to be direct with you: the data from this assessment goes directly into how we target resources, build messaging, and identify the issues that will drive conservative turnout in the critical battleground states.
