The article below is part of Drop Site's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser Media t[o put a focus on rural politics](https://substack.com/redirect/d8928852-6018-4e16-bac6-2ef9620c4e58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a newsletter running through November.
[SIGN UP HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/d8928852-6018-4e16-bac6-2ef9620c4e58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3a8a1695-bea2-4ff8-92aa-d28c35155e6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A demonstrator at an April rally in Traverse City, Michigan, holds a sign emblematic of the growing data center resistance. _(Miles MacClure)_
_Story by Miles MacClure_
Over the past year, dim, windowless, gargantuan warehouses have taken center stage in rural Michigan. The data centers draw ire for consuming vast energy resources to fuel an artificial intelligence boom viewed with increased skepticism. They have spiked utility bills, guzzled the region's fresh water, occupied large tracts of land, and emitted a hum so constant that some residents have sued over excessive noise.
The projects have sparked renewed civic engagement in rural areas and small towns--stories that inspire David and Goliath comparisons. Residents ignite with fury upon finding out their local elected officials have made deals in the dark to bring data centers to town. They come out in force to city council meetings, zoning hearings, and protests in an effort to confront the power of major utility companies and multinational tech corporations with billions of dollars at their disposal.
This growing opposition has forced Michigan's elected officials to reconsider the wisdom of the state's 2024 decision to hand out tax breaks to data center constructors.
Abdul El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and former Wayne County public health official running in the August 4 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, told Barn Raiser that the corporations building data centers aren't straightforward about their development plans.
"There's been so little transparency on the part of the corporations themselves and the part of the utilities," he said. "It has raised the hackles of folks who've learned not to trust a lot of these bigger corporations when they tell them everything's going to be okay."
El-Sayed is locked in a fierce contest that has accentuated divides within the Democratic Party. El-Sayed, whose parents immigrated from Egypt, has pledged not to accept corporate PAC money, has called for eliminating arms sales to Israel and supports universal health care and abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) is a vocal supporter of Israel who has accepted money from corporate PACs, outside groups like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) and has the support of Democratic party leader Sen. Chuck Schumer. Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, a third challenger in the race, suspended her campaign July 5.
An April Emerson College poll shows data centers could be among the deciding issues in the election. Emerson's poll of 519 likely Michigan primary voters found that a majority, or 55%, opposed data centers being built in or near their community, versus 27% who supported them. Opposition to data centers was much higher among likely Democratic primary voters, with 63% opposed versus 45% among likely Republican primary voters.
Dark money spending and support for Israel remains another flashpoint in the campaign, gaining national attention. The Associated Press [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/91db4a24-743e-4a11-88a0-d6f516aaaddb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) AIPAC and its affiliated groups have spent close to $30 million backing Stevens, which is their largest investment ever in a single race.
In January, El-Sayed released a [terms of engagement proposal](https://substack.com/redirect/0113a952-73ca-41c7-b6dc-cefe3679d10e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for data centers, which includes a guarantee for local jobs, a freeze on consumer electricity rate hikes and community benefit agreements. In recent weeks, he has shown support for a system of federal oversight and public ownership of AI companies, a proposal first advanced by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who has endorsed El-Sayed.
Stevens has not laid out any similar positions. At a Democratic primary debate in July, Stevens connected data center construction with job creation, [saying](https://substack.com/redirect/b8db5da7-733b-4793-af81-f4099e7f48f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it will put Michigan "on the forefront of innovation and manufacturing," but she has also called for protecting Michiganders from data center costs.
In an email statement to Barn Raiser, Stevens wrote, "When it comes to data centers and AI infrastructure, my top priority is making sure costs don't go up for Michigan families and that we are protecting good-paying union jobs. We cannot allow utility companies like DTE to pass new costs onto consumers while these projects move forward."
Stevens did not answer the question regarding Michigan residents' concern about AI potentially resulting in less jobs.
" Part of the problem with our politics is too often corporations are buying and selling politicians in the first place. In the case of DTE, our local utility, they've given to 93% of state legislators," said El-Sayed, referencing McMorrow, who eventually dropped out. DTE was McMorrow's [top donor](https://substack.com/redirect/9e356d02-3aa1-4040-992c-b89db6351920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in her 2022 state Senate reelection campaign. El-Sayed's current opponent, Stevens, has [received money](https://substack.com/redirect/ef7564f4-fafc-4ee8-9935-747887eb0594?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from DTE since her first U.S. House reelection campaign in 2020.
McMorrow was among the 38 state senators to vote for a Senate bill that exempted hyperscale data centers from sales and use taxes on their equipment. The bill was signed into law by Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer in 2025.
In hindsight, El-Sayed said a more extensive review process should have occurred before state legislators approved laws to entice data center development in the state.
"I think we should have spent a bit more time to hold the particular utilities accountable ahead of laying out the red carpet, as our state has done," he said.
Data centers have split support amongst unions and their endorsements. The United Auto Workers (UAW), which has over 400,000 members nationwide, endorsed El-Sayed in June. In an April press conference with Bernie Sanders and other labor leaders, UAW president Shawn Fain compared AI to NAFTA because of the risks it poses to workers and communities. "The same greedy corporate power brokers today want us to believe that killing millions of jobs in the name of AI will be a good thing, and the working class knows better," he said. Several of the building trades unions, on the other hand, view data centers as a catalyst for job creation, with many, including Plumbers Local 98 and Pipefitters, Steamfitters, Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Service Local Union 636, having endorsed Stevens.
Michigan's chapter of the AFL-CIO, the nation's largest federation of labor unions, has not made an endorsement in the Senate race. In June, the AFL-CIO released a [policy agenda for the next five years](https://substack.com/redirect/c0d87000-9ce4-4e92-92eb-c132edf4e9db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It included demands that data centers and AI infrastructure be "built by and run on union labor," while requiring that "data centers pay their fair share of costs and taxes" and that working-class families and communities "are protected and included every step of the way, including regulations over water and power use."
Construction workers may be the only local residents who stand to benefit from the data center boom. A Citizens Research Council of Michigan [report](https://substack.com/redirect/01a8195b-e56b-4140-af46-f2325a6019e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on data centers found that the economic benefits of data centers largely occur during the construction phase and concluded that the projects aren't long-term drivers of economic development. In June, _Bloomberg_ [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/0ddf6b2a-666b-4a51-8e63-d263029a81bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that data centers account for 2.3% of all construction spending in the United States.
In a July [debate](https://substack.com/redirect/3b67eb90-c953-4dbb-a242-be1612fa2ba3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), El-Sayed and Stevens clashed over their approaches to AI and data centers. El-Sayed reiterated his community engagement plan and added, "I think we have to be serious about the fact that these pose real dangers," he said. "And the people who are pushing them are the richest, most powerful corporate CEOs in the history of our economy."
Stevens did not speak directly to citizens' concerns about AI but pledged to entice data centers to pay for utilities and rate increases. "I also want to secure Michigan being on the forefront of innovation," she said in a statement to Barn Raiser.
Michigan state Rep. Dylan Wegela (D-Garden City) voted against the tax breaks for data centers when the Michigan House of Representatives voted on the bill in 2023. Wegela had concerns about the environmental impact of data centers from the beginning, he said, but hadn't anticipated the magnitude of the pushback against using hyperscale facilities to drive AI developments.
"I think there are a lot of concerns with that industry right now and concerns about what the technology, unregulated as it is now, might do to working-class people," Wegela said. "And I think that is one of the many reasons this is becoming so controversial now."
For Wegela, data centers are an issue that unites people across party lines. "In areas that these data centers are coming to, you have these coalitions of people on the left and the right coming out to fight together against data centers," he said. "That's working class versus Big Tech."
That coalition of residents was on display on a sunny Saturday morning in Traverse City, Michigan. About 40 protesters showed up to oppose data center construction across Michigan, one of several anti-data center protests that took place across the state on April 11. At the Traverse City protest, attendees brought signs decrying data centers and signs in support of Lake Michigan's freshwater supply. Speakers voiced their opposition to AI in schools and expressed skepticism about the number of local jobs that data centers would generate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8df28123-d6d5-4122-bb95-773d9f42144b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ryan Wagner, the Kalkaska County GOP party chair, speaks at an anti-data center rally in April in Traverse City, Michigan. _(Miles MacClure)_
Ryan Wagner, the Kalkaska County GOP party chair, appeared alongside Mitch Distin, who helped organize the protest and is running as a Democrat for state representative in Michigan's 104th district.
Wagner voiced his discontent with the Make America Great Again movement after continuous campaign promises broken by the Trump administration, like financial gain for working-class Americans, and he found common ground with Democrats seeking to maintain natural resources and oppose AI companies. "I feed my kids off this land. I don't want Big Tech to poison it," Wagner told the crowd.
In November, a company called Rocklocker--a subsidiary of oil and gas company Reefworks--proposed building a data center in rural Kalkaska County, just east of Traverse City, on 1,440 acres of land owned by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources. But community backlash was fierce. At meetings to discuss the proposal, residents didn't buy the economic benefits claimed by Rocklocker and they were wary of the environmental impact.
"The scientific literature is abundantly clear that none of the benefits are distributed or trickle down to local communities, they're the ones who ultimately pay the price for data centers," Distin told the protestors. "The only people who are benefiting from this are big tech CEOs and the legislators."
If a data center is abandoned by a company, it's unclear who will be responsible to pick up the pieces. "What happens if the company goes bankrupt?" said Wegela. "You've seen factories across the state for the automotive industry and cities have been on the hook for cleaning those up or maintaining those. And I just think these are things that aren't being talked about enough."
"Democrats should be leading the opposition to unchecked data center growth," said Michelle Deatrick, chair of the DNC Climate Council. "That's not because we oppose technology, it's because we believe growth needs to serve the public interest, it needs to serve the people, and that's in both the short and the long term."
One tactic used by local organizers has been to implement moratoriums. For instance, residents in Livingston County, north of Detroit, [successfully pushed](https://substack.com/redirect/e5b47320-eabf-4f04-8bb1-50d20abfe85b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Howell Township to approve a six-month moratorium on data center projects, including the $1 billion, 1,077-acre data center proposed backed by Meta, which owns Facebook.
Michigan State Rep. Jennifer Wortz, a Republican in the 35th District, [introduced a bill](https://substack.com/redirect/45755b12-6718-4d12-afc3-c880e844b4d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in February that would place a moratorium on data center construction across the state until April 2027.
Towns, counties, cities, and states across the country are deciding how to respond. An analysis from The Information found more than [300 bans or moratoriums](https://substack.com/redirect/d9b298b2-b2d1-4803-90f0-87768777bf7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across the United States. ([Datacenterbans.com](https://substack.com/redirect/9161153f-d392-4c44-8386-9ead38332423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has an interactive map and updates a tracker on data center policy around the country.) On July 14, New York enacted the nation's first statewide one-year moratorium on data center construction following an executive order signed by Gov. Kathy Hochul. Maine nearly became the first state to do so in April, when the state legislature [passed a moratorium](https://substack.com/redirect/cb12d9ed-09a2-4124-bbb3-a8b7e0e634c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but Gov. Janet Mills, a Democrat, vetoed the bill.
As communities sour on data center projects, they're also turning away from AI. A [Quinnipiac University poll](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac14a05-ebb5-48c5-b15e-eb43c97f6921?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from March 2026 found that 81% of millennials were concerned about AI. The poll also found that 55% of Americans believe AI will do more harm than good, up from 44% in April 2025.
" I don't know if everybody in the public space has connected that the data center and the AI fight is one and the same," said Wegela.
In the workplace, AI is meeting resistance. Futurism [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/837da694-4a7a-4490-aa9c-dd89f5bec80e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that some workers are intentionally sabotaging their employer's AI deployments. Fears over the direction of AI are also turning violent. In April, a Houston man traveled to San Francisco and [hurled a Molotov cocktail ](https://substack.com/redirect/49680f79-f911-42d5-8217-dc38a3a46b09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's house.
"The fear and anxiety about AI is justified," Altman wrote on his [blog](https://substack.com/redirect/9de5c136-acde-4fd0-8ecf-6e1d82174974?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the wake of the attack. "We are in the process of witnessing the largest change to society in a long time, and perhaps ever."
Kyle Blomquist, an architect running for Congress in Michigan's rural 1st congressional district, said the data center tax breaks handed out by Michigan should be repealed. "I'm surprised by the fact that our state has decided to incentivize the location of data centers in the state through these various different tax abatement programs and cuts," said Blomquist.
When Michigan first legalized medical marijuana, local governments had to set ordinances about marijuana store zoning before any business was allowed to set up shop. Blomquist said he would have liked to see a similar process play out with data centers.
Instead, the Wild West of data center growth has exposed a need for towns and counties to update their zoning ordinances. Many of the towns where data centers have been proposed have never had such large developments set up shop before.
" I would've liked more caution with the data centers, more along those lines where you give the communities the opportunity to set their own conditions as to whether or not they want them located there at all," said Blomquist. "Instead, it's kind of a free-for-all."

body:
The mission of this organization has never been more relevant.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260729-1&t=1&akid=3788%2E587540%2EP63tqf)
Peter,
This week, Mitch McConnell reported that he’s still not cleared to return to work in the Senate. **He’s been out since June 14 and has missed at least 38 votes.**
Meanwhile, American employers are still not required to provide paid leave for workers. But apparently the same doesn’t apply for our members of Congress.
Let me be clear: _We aren’t in the business of attacking people for their age or having health issues._ But when we are talking about the leaders of our country, we deserve to know they can do the job we’ve elected them to do, not disappear for weeks or months at a time without even letting the public know what’s going on.
We need leaders who are showing up every day to fight for us. But too many of our politicians have been in office for decades now. Too many of them are completely beholden to special interests and the status quo. And sadly, a significant number of them are at an age where they risk dying in office.
And we know that it’s not just young people who feel this way! Both young and older people are ready to let a new generation lead. To those of you who are of an older generation but support us, I just want to say thank you! Our work would not be possible without this intergenerational coalition of supporters.
And moments like these clearly illustrate how important our mission is. Leaders We Deserve exists to elect the next generation of leaders to drive progress on the most important issues of our time — the affordability crisis, economic inequality, universal health care, worker protections, climate change, and so much more. We exist to elect leaders who can and will actually show up to represent us.

And we know that it’s not just young people who feel this way! Both young and older people are ready to let a new generation lead. To those of you who are of an older generation but support us, I just want to say thank you! Our work would not be possible without this intergenerational coalition of supporters. And moments like these clearly illustrate how important our mission is. Leaders We Deserve exists to elect the next generation of leaders to drive progress on the most important issues of our time — the affordability crisis, economic inequality, universal health care, worker protections, climate change, and so much more. We exist to elect leaders who can and will actually show up to represent us. Thank you, David Hogg

body:
Finally, some good news!
| Fellow Patriot,
---
What a turnaround!
---
After poll after poll showed the Democrats trouncing us in voter enthusiasm all year, the latest polling shows MAGA has finally regained the upper hand!
---
**Newsweek: “MAGA More Motivated Than Democrats for 2026 Midterms: Poll”**

“Trump/MAGA Republicans were the most likely to say they were "definitely going to vote" in the 2026 congressional midterm elections on November 3: **75 percent of MAGA respondents expressed that enthusiasm** [compared to] **63 percent of Democrats.”**
---
The best part? Our Party’s FIRST-EVER Midterm Convention at the end of the summer is the perfect opportunity to boost GOP voter enthusiasm even _further_!
---
__For MAGA, only 75% of our voters being “high propensity” who will “definitely” vote in the midterms is still close to the floor. We need to be aiming for the ceiling, which is 100%!__
---
But before I get ahead of myself, I want to highlight something important:
---
“Voter enthusiasm ahead of an election is... an early indicator of turnout strength and campaign engagement, **_although self-reported voting intention does not necessarily translate into actual turnout.”_ **
---
That last part is why we can’t take our foot off the gas for even a second.
---
**We need to capitalize on this new lead in enthusiasm by verifying every last Republican voter to ensure that they’re a “high propensity” voter who is actually going to show up to vote on – _or before_ – November 3rd. **
---
As long as we do that, we’ll win the midterms!
---
Given the vital importance of voter verification, I took it upon myself to review our Party’s list of voter profiles that were not fully verified as “high propensity” voters.
---
I’ll admit – I was surprised to see your name on there, Fellow Patriot.
---
_That’s why I’m personally reaching out to ask _YOU_ to fully verify your profile. Because if we fully verify the remaining 25% of MAGA voters, our advantage will become insurmountable! _
---

Newsweek: “MAGA More Motivated Than Democrats for 2026 Midterms: Poll” “Trump/MAGA Republicans were the most likely to say they were "definitely going to vote" in the 2026 congressional midterm elections on November 3: 75 percent of MAGA respondents expressed that enthusiasm [compared to] 63 percent of Democrats.” The best part? Our Party’s FIRST-EVER Midterm Convention at the end of the summer is the perfect opportunity to boost GOP voter enthusiasm even further! For MAGA, only 75% of our voters being “high propensity” who will “definitely” vote in the midterms is still close to the floor. We need to be aiming for the ceiling, which is 100%! But before I get ahead of myself, I want to highlight something important: “Voter enthusiasm ahead of an election is... an early indicator of turnout strength and campaign engagement, although self-reported voting intention does not necessarily translate into actual turnout.” That last part is why we can’t take our foot off the gas for even a second. We need to capitalize on this new lead in enthusiasm by verifying every last Republican voter to ensure that they’re a “high propensity” voter who is actually going to show up to vote on – or before – November 3rd. As long as we do that, we’ll win the midterms! Given the vital importance of voter verification, I took it upon myself to review our Party’s list of voter profiles that were not fully verified as “high propensity” voters. I’ll admit – I was surprised to see your name on there, Fellow Patriot. That’s why I’m personally reaching out to ask YOU to fully verify your profile. # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=577%2E127862%2EZzmec7)
Hey there, I'm Berna, Aaron's wife.
I don't usually send emails like this, but campaign season is heating up, and I wanted to reach out myself.
Aaron's been running around non-stop — events, calls, filming, all of it. He'd never say he's stressed. But after thirty years of marriage, I can tell the pressure is building up.
Watching him run this ever-important campaign for governor and fight for people going through exactly what we went through — juggling jobs just to make ends meet and provide for our family — _I couldn't be more proud._
But I also know this work doesn’t come without its anxieties. The campaign’s first TV ad launched this week, and I know Aaron is worried about whether his team will have the resources to keep it on the air.
That's not something I can fix for him on my own. But we can do something good together.
Here's what I'm hoping for: **if enough of you pitch in, we’ll get to tell Aaron that this email brought in a rush of grassroots support. Nothing would make his day more.**
**[Will you help me make that happen by donating $5 or whatever you’re able to today?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260729_1_ak.-3PJbe&amount=5&refcode=em20260729-574&t=3&akid=577%2E127862%2EZzmec7)**

# **Politicians often wait until they 're elected before they start fighting for the people they hope to represent.**
# I don't.
This week, I sent a formal policy letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Secretary of Energy Chris Wright urging the Trump Administration to advance Constitution Pipeline and work with Congress to modernize Section 401 of the Clean Water Act--a law that has allowed one state to hold the energy future of an entire region hostage.
**Why does this matter?**
Because Connecticut families are paying some of the highest electricity costs in America. Those costs ripple through nearly every part of our economy--from higher grocery bills and housing costs to healthcare, manufacturing, and small businesses.
> _Energy isn 't just another political issue. It is the foundation of affordability, opportunity, and economic growth._
Without reliable, affordable energy, Connecticut cannot compete for manufacturers, biotechnology companies, AI facilities, defense contractors, or the next generation of good-paying jobs.
New York recently approved the Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) Pipeline to provide more natural gas for New York City and Long Island.
I support that decision.
But if New York deserves affordable American energy, then Connecticut deserves it too.
We should not accept a system where New York welcomes pipelines that benefit New Yorkers while opposing projects that would help Connecticut families, workers, and businesses.
> That is why I urged Administrator Lee Zeldin and Secretary Chris Wright to move Constitution Pipeline forward and why I called on Congress to modernize Section 401 so environmental laws protect clean water--not become political tools that prevent interstate infrastructure from serving millions of Americans.
As a physician, I understand that reliable energy is essential for hospitals, emergency rooms, nursing homes, pharmacies, and public health.
As an attorney, I understand that lasting solutions require changing the law--not simply issuing press releases.
As your Congressman, I will bring both perspectives to Washington.
This is exactly what I mean when I say I will bring **federal solutions to local problems.**
I am already doing the work.
> I have met with and will continue to meet with federal officials, proposing legislative solutions, and fighting for policies that will make Connecticut more affordable and more competitive. This is not the only energy policy I have submitted and/or discussed with legislators and federal officials.
**Imagine what I can accomplish with a vote in Congress.**
That is why this Republican Primary matters.
On **Tuesday, August 11** , Republicans have a choice.
You can elect someone who is already fighting for Connecticut--or someone who simply talks about the problems.
I am proud to be the **Republican-endorsed candidate for Congress** , and I respectfully ask for your support.
**Fight with me at the Republican Primary on August 11.**
**Vote early August 3 -9 or vote on Primary Day, August 11.**
Together, we can send a fighter to Washington who will never stop working to make Connecticut more affordable, create more opportunity, and deliver real results for our families.
**For a copy of my full letter and press release to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, please email us at[campaigns@goldsteinforcongress.com](https://substack.com/redirect/85a3e6d4-1165-45e4-8781-70ce89c743cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
**Dr. Michael T. Goldstein, M.D., J.D.**

On the trail with Kailee in NY22

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Since my last update, our campaign has continued building momentum across Central New York.We hosted a major day of events with Bruce Blakeman and Republican candidates from across NY-22, drew more than 200 people to a rally in Syracuse, held John Mannion accountable for his costly energy record, and continued taking our message directly to voters through local radio, television and news coverage.I recently joined Jim Reith Unleashed and WRVO’s Campbell Conversations, while NewsChannel 9 covered our rally and POLITICO highlighted the growing importance of energy affordability in this race. Our Facebook community has also grown to more than 3,200 people.Here is a look at what we have been doing and how you can help us keep growing. Thank you for your continued support.-Kailee

| | | | | | | | | | | | **Bruce Blakeman Joins Us in Syracuse**
---
|
---
| | I was proud to host Republican candidate for Governor Bruce Blakeman for a full day across Syracuse alongside GOP candidates and local leaders from throughout NY-22.
We started with breakfast at the Gem Diner, met farmers and vendors at the Central New York Regional Market, visited Syracuse Nationals, and stopped at St. Patrick’s Irish Fest on Tipp Hill.
We finished the day with a rally of more than 200 supporters. It was an incredible show of energy for our campaign and the entire Republican ticket across Central New York.
[**WATCH NEWSCHANNEL 9’S COVERAGE**](https://us.list-manage.com/kQEHS3DQ_at?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**What Is Happening in This Race**
---
| |

John Mannion is already trying to define me before many voters have heard directly from me.Here is the truth: I grew up in Auburn, came home to raise my family, and have spent my career working on agriculture, food affordability and policies affecting working families. I will work with members of either party to deliver results, and I will always explain my votes directly to the people I represent.Meanwhile, Mannion still owes voters explanations for his own record. He voted against keeping the government open, opposed a congressional stock-trading ban, and supported Albany energy policies that have increased costs, and voted to eliminate $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel—siding with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez even as Hakeem Jeffries and a bipartisan House majority rejected the effort. POLITICO recently put a national spotlight on how Mannion’s energy record has become the defining issue in NY-22. I also released a detailed memo outlining his votes for mandates affecting natural gas, construction, vehicles, farmland and local communities.

[READ THE POLITICO ENERGY REPORT](https://us.list-manage.com/sUylsM9OmGi?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)[READ THE FULL ENERGY MEMO](https://us.list-manage.com/Bf4RhqUsmC9?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
[READ ABOUT HIS VOTE TO DEFUND ISRAEL](https://us.list-manage.com/ACIOPA4x30Q?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **In the Media**
---
| | We are taking our message directly to voters. Recent appearances and coverage included:
[**Jim Reith Unleashed:**](https://us.list-manage.com/3ATGP7YjFGx?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843) Term limits, taxes, energy affordability, bipartisanship and my commitment to explaining every vote.
[**Bob Lonsberry Show:**](https://us.list-manage.com/1DBWaO4AMGv?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)**** Discussing Mannion’s support for tax increases and climate policies, and my plan to lower costs.
[**WRVO’s Campbell Conversations:** ](https://us.list-manage.com/NSrWL9HXBRc?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)My background, the affordability crisis, housing, energy and why I am running for Congress.
[**Syracuse.com:**](https://us.list-manage.com/X5A8QoXuLqC?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843) “I’ve been in those rooms watching Central New York get left behind in D.C.,” Buller said. “So, I’m going to come here and fight like hell because I know how the process works.”

Peter, [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136237778/636790635/644753417?amount=10&source=DWS_EM_FR_072926_B1_Pappas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNTk1MjkyMy03YzhiLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uSeLMcB2FpWV159neIaaPF5Ff4AG9SqUnwlYjFv6kaU=) _Josh Rogers/NHPR_ In the GOP primary debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken restaurant." He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about. **I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.** My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter — because they do. **John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life.** He was born into the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan that sells minerals to China. That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.” New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is running to protect people like himself. **I'm running for everyone else.** He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he doesn’t represent us. | | | Peter, I need to be honest with you about where this race stands. See above. Cash is king, but in a major Senate race like ours cash-on-hand (meaning, money in our bank account that we can spend) is king... _And the numbers are looking bad ..._ **Right now, James Talarico has $21.5 million cash on hand in the bank. We have $6.9 million cash on hand.** That gap is serious, and it matters -- because right now, today, he is on television in nearly every major market in Texas and we cannot answer him... Cash on hand is not a political talking point. It is the difference between being heard and being drowned out. Every dollar given today will have a massive impact... And every dollar ungiven widens the gap and increases the Democrats' chances for unleashing chaos... **On top of that ...**Three separate polls show this race tied. Cook Political Report just downgraded us. The national media is starting to write the story they want to write... _We cannot let them write it. We need to change the narrative now!_ This race is decided right now, in the next 72 hours, by people like you who decide whether to step up or sit it out... **_Will you help right now?_** Remember, I have spent my career fighting for Texas. clean_body: Please keep this one confidential- thanks. | | | | | | | Peter, I need to be honest with you about where this race stands. See above. Cash is king, but in a major Senate race like ours cash-on-hand (meaning, money in our bank account that we can spend) is king... And the numbers are looking bad ... Right now, James Talarico has $21.5 million cash on hand in the bank. We have $6.9 million cash on hand. That gap is serious, and it matters -- because right now, today, he is on television in nearly every major market in Texas and we cannot answer him... Cash on hand is not a political talking point. It is the difference between being heard and being drowned out. Every dollar given today will have a massive impact... And every dollar ungiven widens the gap and increases the Democrats' chances for unleashing chaos... On top of that ...Three separate polls show this race tied. Cook Political Report just downgraded us. The national media is starting to write the story they want to write... We cannot let them write it. We need to change the narrative now! This race is decided right now, in the next 72 hours, by people like you who decide whether to step up or sit it out... Will you help right now? Remember, I have spent my career fighting for Texas. I have gone up against the federal government, the open border lobby, and the entire weight of the Washington establishment -- and I have not backed down once. I am not backing down now! But I need you with me, Peter. I am proud to be in this fight alongside you. Let's keep pushing for Texas and America! Peter,
It’s Alex Vindman, humbly asking you to chip in a donation of $10 to my Senate campaign in Florida. America needs a leader who has a track record of taking on tough fights and can turn our country around in this critical moment. That is why I am asking:
$10 to help reach undecided Florida voters with our new ads, before Donald Trump’s allies do.
$10 to stand up against the attacks from the billionaires and special interest groups, who are spending whatever it takes to protect Ashley Moody.

We're facing the repercussions of the partisan election takeover laws that went into effect at the end of 2024, Team.
To refresh your memory: After the 2024 elections and the defeat of a MAGA candidate for governor, opponents of voting rights in North Carolina jammed through a bill that took the power of the governor to appoint people to election boards and handed that to the state auditor . It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites at several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.
We have to fight these suppressive actions in North Carolina and any other state where opponents of voting rights try to replicate this. Western Carolina University in Jackson County, for example, has had a polling place on campus since 2016 that’s been used in five general elections and four primaries, according to a document prepared for the board. The state board voted 3-2 to get rid of it.
Closing the campus voting site would not save money, but “ would create barriers to voting for young, rural residents ,” Jackson County Board member Betsy Swift told the state board. 64% of students don’t have vehicles to drive to the polling place, she said.
Without the on-campus site, the closest polling place for students will be a recreation center nearly two miles away. Students without transportation will have to walk along a four-lane highway and through a meadow to get there.

body:
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5565%2E35263%2E0II2Ha)
Peter, have you heard my coming out story?
I first came out in college. Back then, I worried that living my authentic life openly would mean giving up any chance of running for office one day.
Turns out, I didn't have to choose.
I watched people across our LGBTQ+ community show real courage — coming out, living openly, being public about who they are. They showed me I could do both: run for office, and be honest about who I am.
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260729-personalstory.r-sUpc&amount=5&refcode=&t=2&akid=5565%2E35263%2E0II2Ha)
Because of that support and those acts of courage, I became the first openly gay U.S. Senator in our nation’s history.
**But I didn't run to make history. I ran to make a difference for Wisconsinites.**
And that's exactly what we've done — bolstering manufacturing, standing up for veterans, lowering prescription drug costs. I've gotten to do all of it while showing up as my true, authentic self, every single day.
I’m so grateful for the thousands of activists who have fought for representation. Together, we're stronger. And together, we're not done fighting yet.
In solidarity,
Tammy

| | Dear David, Hereʼs a picture I took this morning of Carleigh getting the kids ready for camp. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/uuceQ_uPrq4OGF5X7Ivn6g~~/AAUS1hA~/xtQ7lwFnnxmeY-a4s60ARZcMmhkLZddpaSP_zZ0lUg-czAJrVkKrsR41l5I-IBWxiWcBcHhMMgAidSp0GUojQbaeDSUtZBnrz5wyctfg8OCBriNsnulLB_yW8GJuac3OL6-JMdMnW3F7Cu9-_55FOi2Q6e2h57vNtusLW4w06aRm1q7-BH9kb5eCTYSqoUTj8iguPM73bVQX4zr6kHx5LSitIZzDDzArPUoNKpdUirqWuSDjgCX9Z_NkxGDSdNXZvkD5RsmwR43MkfKAS4mesw~~) This is our life, and in so many ways it is completely ordinary. Two kids in public school, neighbor-kids playing in the backyard on a summer evening, bills that keep coming from the doctor even though the insurance company promised us they'd fix the coding error, never knowing what to cook for dinner... And thatʼs exactly what she did.** And here she is... here WE are. Our little family, our little neighborhood, our amazing seaside town, and literally thousands of people who have joined Carleigh in the belief that we can organize, build power, and make change. The midterm elections are coming up fast, and Democrats have real opportunities to take back power across the country.

Hi, I want to level with you:
If you’re upset that Republicans like Jon Husted are only serving billionaires and corporate special interests in the U.S. Senate – not working people – I get it.
If you’re angry about how the rich keep getting richer while working families fight to stretch every paycheck, I understand. Completely.
If you’re looking for a way to do something about it, **please hear me out.**
I’m ready to kick Husted out of office and give Ohioans a senator who will put them first. I’m running my campaign the right way, with grassroots support from folks like you.
**Not only is our fight for working people riding on this race – but also the future of Senate control. If we lose here, we can all but say goodbye to our chances of taking back the majority.**
I know we can win, but it’s going to be expensive. And while some politicians rely on big checks from billionaires and executives, I don’t – because I don’t answer to them. I answer to you.
So today, ahead of our end-of-month deadline, I’m turning to the folks who truly understand the stakes of this race and want to change our country for the better, with a chance to help.

subject: I’m proud to endorse Ryan McLaren.

body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Dear Peter,
I've gotten to know Ryan McLaren over the last several months, and I can honestly say he's exactly the kind of leader Vermont needs right now.
That's why I'm proud to endorse him for Lieutenant Governor of Vermont.
Will you split a contribution of $10 or more between Ryan McLaren and my campaign to help elect a leader who has spent his life fighting for others? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729&amount=10]
DONATE $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729&amount=10]
DONATE MORE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729]
Ryan grew up in Vermont, attended its public schools, served in AmeriCorps, coached youth lacrosse, and has spent the past decade serving Vermonters on Senator Peter Welch's staff.
In 2017, a skiing accident left Ryan with a spinal cord injury, and doctors told him he might never walk again.
That injury became part of who Ryan is, and strengthened the leader he would become.
Step by step, he fought his way back—not just to walk again, but to return to public service with even greater determination.
Ryan doesn't just talk about resilience. He's lived it.
Now he's running for Lieutenant Governor because he knows too many Vermont families are struggling just to get by. Housing costs are soaring. Child care is out of reach for too many parents. Working families deserve leaders who know what it means to face hardship—and refuse to give up.
This seat is one of Democrats' best opportunities to flip statewide power in Vermont. But it will take a strong grassroots campaign to get it done.
Please split a contribution between Ryan McLaren and my campaign today to help elect a leader who knows what it means to fight back and never give up. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729]
DONATE $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729&amount=10]
DONATE MORE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-ryan-mclaren-fundraising-split?refcode=20260729]
At a moment when too many people have lost faith in politics, Ryan reminds us what public service is supposed to look like: humility, perseverance, and putting people first.
I'm proud to stand with him, and I hope you'll join me.
In solidarity,
Ro

#
Hey Peter,
In the 2018 elections, Democrats took control of the House. In 2020, Democrats took back the White House. And just a few months later in 2021, the Georgia runoff gave Democrats the Senate.
That wave of victory has a real impact on the lives of millions of Americans. But in 2024, the Trump GOP fought back – and they peeled much of that progress away.
Now in 2026, after Democrats have already overworked in elections across the country, it’d be easy to think things are already heading in the right direction. But if the last ten years should have taught us anything, it’s that **we CANNOT afford to take anything for granted.**
**[That’s why today, we’re asking you to chip in toward efforts to support Democrats across the country. For much of the last year, Democrats have only been gaining in the polls. As recently as May, RCP’s congressional polling average had Democrats up nearly 8% over Republicans – doubling the lead RCP’s average had for Democrats eight years earlier, in May 2018!
But in 2018, Democrats worked to keep building on their lead – and together, they took their lead from 4% in May to 8% in July. In 2026, it’s been the reverse – after the Trump GOP started spending their record-breaking billionaire-funded war chest this year, the lead for Democrats has dropped from 8% to under 5% within just a few short weeks... And after 18 months of GOP-led midterm gerrymandering, that makes things even harder for Democrats this November than they were in 2018.
Democrats have got to turn things around – and to do that, they’ll need volunteers, grassroots supporters, candidates, and campaigns to all work together just like we did in 2018. Friend,

Over 45,000 federal employees — and two to three times that in contractors — call Maryland's Third Congressional District home. They keep our families healthy, our environment safe, and our national security strong. But right now, even after the sledgehammer of DOGE, civil service protections remain under steady political threat. Just last week, we fought for civilian DoD employees to maintain their collective bargaining rights in this year’s annual defense authorization bill.

Will you chip in $25 right now to help fuel our campaign as we stand up for Maryland's public servants? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-July2026-FR-CivilService?&refcode=E30952-20260729-CivilService-SL-Trump&amount=25]

This issue is deeply personal to me. Both of my parents were civil servants, so I grew up seeing firsthand the dedication and sacrifice that goes into a life of service. That's why I introduced bipartisan legislation to protect probationary employees and the future of the civil service. Hardworking, dedicated federal employees should never be used as bargaining chips in political games.

Defending our workforce takes a strong, well-funded grassroots campaign that can mobilize voters and ensure local families are protected.

Our team relies on support from people like you to keep organizing across Howard, Anne Arundel, and Carroll counties. Please consider pitching in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to support our work and defend our public servants. Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. Yet he just keeps begging.

### **We 've endorsed over 100+ Black candidates! Now, we need to help them win.**
* * *
In 2026 alone, The Collective PAC has endorsed over 100+ Black candidates at every level of government.
That means 100+ more bold leaders who are ready to fight for our rights, uplift our communities, and build a truly equitable democracy.
But endorsing these candidates is only the beginning.
To win their races, they need staff, resources, infrastructure, and grassroots support.

That's why we're recruiting candidates, training leaders, investing directly in campaigns, and building the infrastructure needed to win races up and down the ballot.
**And we depend on grassroots support to make that work possible.**
Every dollar donated helps fund our voter outreach, candidate support, and campaign operations needed to build Black political power.
**[We set a $20,000 End-Of-Month goal to keep this work moving forward. So, will you please donate to help us turn 100 endorsements into 100 victories on Election Day?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/206a3ed5-eb2d-4bf1-955d-6a2cf71e5aba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

### **President Obama Sounded the Alarm. We 're Answering the Call.**
* * *
Electing Black candidates hinges on mobilizing voters, organizers, and supporters.
And President Barack Obama recently reminded us how important it is to take action.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/206a3ed5-eb2d-4bf1-955d-6a2cf71e5aba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So here at The Collective PAC, we are answering that call by investing in the candidates, campaign talent, and voters who can lead us forward.
-> We've trained more than 2,000 operatives across the country, helping to build the next generation of Black leaders.
-> We're investing in Black candidates who understand the needs of our communities and are ready to deliver meaningful change.
-> And we're organizing Black and Brown voters across the country who will help us make history this November.
This work is essential to electing the Black candidates we've endorsed.
Because an endorsement can help launch a campaign, but it takes organizers, strategists, volunteers, and voters to win it.
And all of that work requires resources.
That's why our $20,000 End-Of-Month goal is so important. It'll ensure our candidates have the support they need during the most critical months of their campaigns.
**[So, if you 're ready to answer President Obama's call, will you chip in $9 right now to elect the next wave of Black leaders?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/206a3ed5-eb2d-4bf1-955d-6a2cf71e5aba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

### **The Supreme Court won 't stop us from building Black political power.**
* * *
We need to build strong, lasting infrastructure to overcome the barriers Black communities continue to face.
Recent Supreme Court rulings have made it harder for Black and Brown voters to challenge discriminatory maps and protect the full power of their votes.
And these decisions have created real obstacles to fair representation - but won't let them stop us.
Here at The Collective PAC, we're responding by investing in robust, on-the-ground voter turnout operations in states where Republicans are undermining our right to vote.
Because when the path to fair representation becomes more difficult, we don't give up.
* We organize more voters.
* We support more candidates.
* We build stronger campaigns.
* And we invest more heavily in the communities that deserve to be heard.

But with the 2026 Midterms right around the corner, there has never been a more urgent time to act.
The investments we make right now will determine how many candidates we can support, how many voters we can reach, and how many Black Democrats we can help elect.
That's why hitting our $20,000 End-Of-Month fundraising goal is so critical.

Dear Peter, **Today we stood up for your voice, and your future.** I was proud to be in Boston to represent you, the Maine voter. In 2024 we overwhelmingly supported limiting contributions to Super PACs through a statewide citizens referendum. This initiative received more total votes than any other issue ever on the Maine ballot, a clear sign that Mainers are fed up with a political system corrupted by dark money and special interests. Maine elections should be decided by Maine voters, not by out-of-state dark money groups with no transparency and no accountability. But too often our voices are drowned out by multi-million-dollar megaphones. Three out of four Maine voters said they want limits on Super PAC money. Yet now, the very interests this law was designed to stop are suing to preserve their power. This fight is about more than one law. It is about defending the will of the people. It is about protecting our elections from the corrupting influence of dark money special interests. **And it is about whether our democracy is still truly of, by, and for the people.** I’m proud to stand alongside Maine voters and with citizens across our country in the fight to take back our elections and protect our democracy. Our campaign is fueled by ordinary Mainers like you, not dark money Super PACs. Thank you for being part of this effort. Now more than ever we need your help. [If you are able to give any amount, thank you. ](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=oral_arguments_7_29&n=1) If you have already given, thank you. _**"Deb Haaland Criticizes Trump Administration’s Effort to Roll Back Chaco Canyon Protections"**_
Friend, Jane Fonda here.

Deb and I have been in the climate fight together for years, and I can say with my whole heart that she's exactly the kind of leader I had in mind when I launched the Jane Fonda Climate PAC.

[**She's never stopped fighting to protect our public lands, our climate, and our communities, and I know she won't stop as New Mexico's next Governor.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1131-fr-nd&t=1&akid=11374%2E400544%2EX7ZqXF)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1131-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11374%2E400544%2EX7ZqXF)
---
**No fight better shows the kind of leader Deb is than her commitment to protect Chaco Canyon.
**
In Congress, Deb fought to protect the lands surrounding Chaco from new oil and gas development.

Then, as Secretary of the Interior, she helped secure protections for the sacred cultural landscape that so many Tribal communities have fought to preserve.
Throughout her time at Interior, she also helped protect more land and water than any administration in U.S. history while creating good-paying jobs in clean energy, conservation, and cleaning up legacy pollution.

**Now Donald Trump and his administration are determined to slash protections for the lands surrounding Chaco Canyon and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling, threatening one of the most significant cultural landscapes in the world.
**
That's why we need a leader in New Mexico who listens to her community and never hesitates to put people above corporate greed.

[**If you're ready to elect a Governor who will stand up to Donald Trump and protect our sacred places, will you consider making a donation of any amount today to help elect Deb as the next Governor of New Mexico?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1131-fr-nd&t=3&akid=11374%2E400544%2EX7ZqXF)

In January 2020, as the number of cases of Covid-19 in the U.S. began to rise, Fauci quickly took control of the narrative. As early as Jan. 23, he began making detailed lists of his media appearances.

He also claimed that it was an "amazing" day for himself, despite the rising concerns about American citizens' exposure to the virus.
The speed at which Fauci jumps between discussing death tolls and his own raising popularity is stunningly dystopian. At the height of lockdowns on March 15, Fauci mentions that there have been 58 deaths in the U.S. thus far, before immediately bragging that he did "all 5 Sunday shows." On March 19, as cases continued to surge, he complains that the POTUS "had a press conference which did not include me." The situation with my national and international fame is explosive and really unimaginable. Fauci's self obsession becomes comical throughout the course of the pandemic. He progresses from merely compiling articles about his work with the pandemic, to collecting magazine covers, photos of street art, and HBO television series rumors that bolster his public image.
The diary also shows how Fauci's desire for power expands throughout the course of the pandemic. On May 23, he again complained about the Trump administration's frustration with him, chalking it up to Fauci "becoming a star that outshine [Trump]." A few paragraphs later, he praises himself for there being "an amazing firestorm about me on tv tonight", and gushing over Chris Cuomo for telling people "we need Fauci." # [Friends, I'm a geek.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=208995708&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4OTk1NzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODUzNTkyNDIsImV4cCI6MTc4Nzk1MTI0MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.AHRDHaxai889CA3MXkb8kS39PXS2CQKIFYCxJqLhFrY)
### "Stevens has some late momentum."
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 29

---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/friends-im-a-geek?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4OTk1NzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODUzNTkyNDIsImV4cCI6MTc4Nzk1MTI0MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.AHRDHaxai889CA3MXkb8kS39PXS2CQKIFYCxJqLhFrY&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/friends-im-a-geek?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends, I'm a geek.
It's true. Most people who've met me or who get this Substack aren't even a skosh surprised by that admission.
From manufacturing policy to jobs reports to voter data, I'm a gal who loves getting into the numbers. So I was especially interested when fellow numbers nerd Nate Silver published a whole deep-dive on our Senate race.
Nate Silver said, "Stevens has some late momentum," and cited a couple of polls that show we're leading the primary.
Let me nerd out for a minute and walk you through what he found, because I want this grassroots team to understand what's happening, especially with the primary in just six days. You deserve to see the numbers I'm seeing and know how I'm thinking about all of this.
**A new poll has us up by 7 points against MAGA Republican Mike Rogers.** The Glengariff Group polled our primary for _The Detroit News_ and found us leading 48 to 41. That's good news because we're leading (obviously), but it's also important to note that this is an independent, A-rated pollster, and a 7-point lead.
**Mallory McMorrow 's supporters are joining this grassroots team in large numbers.** When Mallory suspended her campaign, the question was where her folks would go. And I want to say something directly to those folks, because I know some of you are reading this: Welcome. I know it's tough to have your candidate drop out, but I'm glad you're here. Mallory has been an important voice, both in this race and in the State Senate. She made me a better candidate, and I look forward to working with her in the future to build a stronger Michigan.
**The endorsements are coming. And I 'm grateful.** Governor Gretchen Whitmer. Senator Gary Peters. Congressman Jim Clyburn. I'm truly honored beyond words.
**The general election numbers are popping.** Looking at the highest-rated pollsters in Michigan, I'm beating MAGA Mike Rogers, while my primary opponent trails him. And that's similar to what _The Cook Political Report_ said: "If El-Sayed wins the primary, Democrats have little chance of holding the seat."
That's the state of the race, friends. Not according to me. According to the numbers and the people whose entire job and reputation is about trying to get this stuff right.
But **polls can only take you so far. They aren 't a prediction or a prophecy.**
These polls tell us we're headed in the right direction. But polls don't vote. Newsletters don't vote. And numbers nerds only get you so far.
People vote. And Michiganders are voting right now - ballots are filled out at kitchen tables across this state and going back in the mail as I type this. We are six days from the primary on Aug. 4. A day when so much will be decided. Which party has the best chance of controlling the Senate. Whether we can put a real check on Donald Trump. Whether we fight for reproductive freedom, Social Security, affordable gas and groceries, health insurance. Everything.
**I don 't want to wake up on Aug. 5 with a single regret, and I don't want you to either.** I want us to be able to say we put absolutely everything on the line when it mattered. That's what "late momentum" really is. It's not a permission slip to sit back, it's an assignment. A goal. A chance to show what this grassroots team is about.
Here's my ask: Will you help me build on this momentum? If you're able, chip in $20 or whatever you can to help us finish these last 6 days with our foot on the gas. Knocking on more doors, making more calls, getting more air time for our ads, and more of everything that got us here.
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/69a54a03-efcf-4305-bf62-b5ff4fcde7a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's give Nate Silver something to write about on Aug. 5. Let's tell the story of how our late momentum surged and how we're now on track to keep Michigan blue and flip the Senate.
I'm ready to get that newsletter.
More soon.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/69a54a03-efcf-4305-bf62-b5ff4fcde7a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

name: Scott Wiener
subject: what happened at the Trans March
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott WIENER FOR CONGRESS
body:
| |

Hi Peter,

Last month, I went to the San Francisco Trans March, as I have since it began more than two decades ago.

A group of people surrounded me, harassed me, and told me I was no longer queer. I left because I could no longer safely remain.

No one gets to erase who I am. And no one gets to erase my record.

I wrote California’s transgender refuge law, which protects families who come here because another state is threatening to prosecute them or take away their children for seeking gender-affirming care. That law became a model for states across the country.

I wrote laws protecting transgender people in prison, establishing an LGBTQ Seniors Bill of Rights, and expanding access to HIV prevention medication.

I have been fighting for our community since I came out during the AIDS crisis. I will keep fighting for trans people, whether it is politically easy or brutally hard.

In the four days after the Trans March, 1,070 people contributed $127,600 to this campaign. That outpouring meant more to me than I can express.

If you were one of them, thank you. [**If not, I hope you’ll join us before we close the books on July Friday night.**

**The bullies and bigots are still coming for us. Every contribution, whether it’s $1 or $100, represents another person standing with this movement. Hey Peter,
The end of July is quickly approaching, which means that the election is going to be here soon! I can't believe the progress that we’ve made, winning a primary and raising over $1 million. I wouldn’t be where I am without your support.
Each passing day, we get one step closer to flipping NC-13 blue and sending our corrupt, overconfident congressional representative, Brad Knott, home for good. Things are working in our favor, and I could not be more excited.
So here are the facts:
1. More voters participated in the Democratic primary than the Republican primary this year.
This is exciting because we now know that more Democratic voters are participating and more unaffiliated voters are voting in Democratic primaries, which means they’re more likely to vote blue in November!
2. This campaign has raised the most money and has the most volunteers for this district.
By showing up strong every single month and the dedication of our hardworking volunteers, we have the strongest supporters helping our campaign in this district.
3. National polling shows that there may be a blue wave coming, and Trump’s approval rating is underwater (by a lot) in our district.
We all know Washington isn't working for us anymore, so something needs to change. Even in this district, which voted for Trump in 2024, polls have shown that he is significantly underwater. My opponent, Brad Knott, is endorsed by, and rides the coattails of, the current administration.
Based on all of these facts, we’re on the right track. We just need to keep showing strength every single month, making sure we have all the resources we need to inform voters about how critical this race is. With July coming to an end in just a few days, can I count on your donation to help us finish this month strong? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260729] Anything you can afford to give will help us keep scaling up so that we can reach our neighbors and flip this seat.

Hey,
Let's run through the tape real quick:
**The first major play:** I won our primary and became the official Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Iowa.
**The next key move:** Cook Political Report moved Iowa in our direction, citing my strength as a candidate and the energy we've built on the ground.
**Then, the big twist:** _Fox News_ debuted their first 2026 Senate forecast this week, **and they rate Iowa a Toss-Up.**
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260729_3.gtC0T_&refcode=em20260729-3&t=1&akid=8008%2E582294%2EnKjM_1)

**Read that again.** _Fox News_ is telling their own viewers that this race is a dead heat. Because it is.
Just 4 seats in the entire country made their Toss-Up column, and Iowa, a state Trump won by 13 points, is one of them.
_My Republican opponent, Ashley Hinson, didn't want to wake up to that headline._

**Iowa isn't a lock for the GOP anymore. It's a genuine fight, and I intend to win it.**

name: Douglas Alexander
subject: live debate/discussion with the incumbent, Mark Pocan, at 10:00 CST tomorrow, Thursday, July 30
body:
Greetings my fellow citizens who have signed up for my email newsletter! Thank you for doing so; I hope to meet, or meet again, many of you in the months to come. I apologize for being so very late with some of you. It is a challenge determining how best to spend my time, but I definitely have been tardy with some of you.

However, I'm excited to tell you that I’ll be participating in a live debate/discussion with the incumbent, Mark Pocan, at 10:00 CST tomorrow, Thursday, July 30, on WCLO radio in Janesville, WI. To listen to it live, choose one of these four options:
1. AM 1230 or FM 92.7
2. Download the "Big Radio Ap" to your cell phone
3. Go to www.wclo.com and click “Listen Live”
4. It should also be available via Amazon Echo devices via “Tune in” (whatever that is!)

To listen to it later, there is a podcast, but you won’t find it via your cell phone podcast ap. To find it:
* Open the "Big Radio Ap" on your cell phone, click “Podcasts” at the top (as opposed to “live streams”) and find it there.
* Or, go to www.wclo.com and click “podcast,” then “Your Talk Show Podcasts.”

It supposedly will be posted ~15 minutes after the show ends.

Douglas Alexander
608-843-1075
[AlexanderForHope.com](http://AlexanderForHope.com)
X: @Dglas4TermLimts

...It's time to get serious about getting the Career Politicians out of Congress.

name: Office of U.S. Senator Raphael Warnock
subject: Stopping the Spread of Private Equity in Housing
body:
|
---
Dear Neighbor,

I'm excited to announce that legislation I've authored to stop private equity from mass-purchasing homes is now law. This ban will stop the spread of Wall Street firms from buying up single-family homes and help bring the American Dream within reach for thousands of Georgians.

Earlier this month, I was in Atlanta's Adamsville neighborhood speaking to lifelong Georgia residents who were struggling to purchase a home. One of those Georgians was Jacob Parcel, father of two and owner of Soulful Shears barbershop. Jacob and his wife had been trying for years to buy a house, but they, like many Georgians, have had to compete with Wall Street firms bulk-buying homes and outbidding first-time home buyers.

I believe that homes are for people, not corporations. That's why I pushed for Congress to finally protect everyday Georgians like Jacob instead of billionaires and wealthy corporate investors.
Last week, I met Jacob Parcel, a third-generation Georgian, and his son. Jacob and his wife have been trying for years to purchase a home and worry they may need to look out of state
After a year of effort, my legislation to stop the spread of private equity was included as part of the _21st Century ROAD to Housing Act_ , which became law earlier this month. This bipartisan legislation is the first housing bill to pass Congress in nearly two decades. This law also includes provisions to increase Georgia's housing supply by cutting through red tape that blocks housing developments before they even start, expand access to affordable housing, and [improve the efficiency of the nation's federal housing programs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16724.25460111.9193170.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.warnock.senate.gov%2fwp-content%2fuploads%2f2026%2f06%2f06.23.26-COMMS-Warnock-ROAD-to-Housing-Priorities-1.pdf&redir_log=628449358902740).

More good news: I secured a provision in this housing bill to ensure all Georgians can request a second appraisal to ensure everyone is given a fair estimate of their home's market value before they put it up for sale.
[](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16724.25460111.9193170.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2freel%2f971546192381100&redir_log=335292893963269) [WATCH](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16724.25460111.9193170.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2freel%2f971546192381100&redir_log=335292893963269): Stopping the spread of private equity in Georgia
As one of twelve kids who grew up in public housing, I understand the dignity and security housing provides, which is why I will continue to work with my colleagues across the aisle to help Georgians afford rent and purchase a home.

Although this law is a great first step in addressing the housing crisis, there is more work to be done. Georgians need more action from Washington, and as a U.S. Senator for all Georgians, it is the honor of my life to continue to fight for you and our great state. Keep the faith, and keep looking up.
U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock

| This is official correspondence from the Office of Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock. If you have any questions, please contact our office [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenWarnock&crop=16724.25460111.9193170.14245539&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.warnock.senate.gov%2fcontact%2fcontact-form%2f&redir_log=51402161759365).

clean_body: | Roy Cooper, Mary Peltola, James Talarico, Josh Turek, Sherrod Brown — and so many others — are giving Democrats a fighting chance to win back the Senate. Derek, in just a moment, I'm going to lay out the stakes of this election and make sure we're all on the same page about what Democrats need to do to win in November. Control of the Senate comes down to a net gain of four seats. Republicans know it as well as we do, and they are not planning to hold their majority by virtue of their policies and arguments. They are planning to outspend us. Dark money donors. Handpicked self-funders. Super PACs behind every vulnerable Republican on the map. And we know what a Republican majority does with its oversight power, because we have watched it sit unused for two years. They will do nothing. A president has personally taken in billions since taking office, and this Senate has not asked him or his cronies a single question about it under oath. He has gone after the machinery of elections themselves, and this Senate has called it overreach to object. A Senate that will not use its subpoena power is a Senate that has decided the president answers to no one. We must flip four seats to take power, and there are eight places to get them — North Carolina, Ohio, Maine, Alaska, Iowa, Florida, Mississippi and Texas. Every one is winnable and not one is safe. A year ago most people looking at this map would have said we had a brutal path. That changed because candidates decided to run in states that were not supposed to be competitive. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240980%2E444211%2EVHQn9X)
I wish it were not so, but we are still in a legal battle with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.
He sued me and Powered by People last year to try to stop me from speaking against the Republican gerrymander of five Texas congressional districts and to stop our organization from doing the effective registration and turnout work that could spell his defeat in November’s senate contest.
While we have won at the district and appeals court level (where the Republican justices reprimanded Paxton for his attack on my First Amendment rights), we are not out of the woods yet.
More court dates and more attacks from Paxton.
And that means more money that we must spend to defend ourselves and take the fight to him. We must win both so that we can continue to work and so that it is clear that our government cannot intimidate or silence the voices it disagrees with.
These fights have cost us more than $500,000 so far.
[**Please make a contribution today to ensure we have the resources to finally defeat Ken Paxton in court and continue our important organizing work on the ground.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260729.aWoke9&refcode=ema20260729-240980&t=3&akid=240980%2E444211%2EVHQn9X)
Thank you,
Beto

name: Mike Rogers
subject: This is the hardest email I’ve had to write
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rogers for Senate
body:
This goes far beyond politics. The fabric of America is unweaving. | | | | | A Personal Message From Mike
---
Friend,
---
I am reaching out to you directly because, quite frankly, I don't know where else to turn. I've spent the last few hours pacing the room, trying to process what is happening. The latest developments are incredibly daunting, and my heart is heavy with an overwhelming sense of urgency.

I grew up in a working-class family in Allagash.
We didn’t always have heat or running water. Sometimes, we relied on food assistance to make ends meet.
My dad was a logger out in the woods, and one day he and his fellow loggers had to stand up to a wealthy landowner who was threatening their wages. They weren’t even asking for more money, they just wanted to be paid fairly.
“Take the pay cut or go home,” they were told.
I’ll never forget that day. I was only 11 years old, and watched my dad fight for something bigger than all of us — a basic fairness every worker should be entitled to, the ability to make ends meet, the ability to put food on the table for their family.
I know what it’s like to worry about paying the bills on time. I know what it’s like to fight, not just for your own future, but for the future of everyone around you, too.
And it’s that fight I’ll bring to the United States Senate. For too long, our voices have been ignored and crushed by powerful corporations and special interests who make backroom deals with greedy politicians.
Now’s our chance to change that. NAME, we have less than 100 days to build a campaign big enough to defeat Susan Collins. But with your help today, I know we can do it. I promise you I’ll spend every day in the Senate fighting for you and your families.
So that’s why I have to ask: Can you chip in a donation of any amount split between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to defeat Collins and take back our Democratic majority? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
I appreciate your support always,
Troy

When her father became seriously ill and lost his health insurance, her family struggled to afford the care he needed.
